**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Native retries, logs, vendor support and configuration reviews are often sufficient.

## Bounded deliverable
Analyze sample execution history and plan limits; model polling and branching cost.

**Pilot cap:** One platform bill/sample, one workflow and three volume scenarios.

Include a versioned field/rule map, sanitized export where permitted, test results, known limitations, rollback/recovery instructions and customer-owned handover. Changes outside the cap need a new estimate. No external publication, unsolicited messaging, payments/refunds, destructive data changes or account-wide permissions are implied.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence
1. Confirm the current behavior, ownership, destination semantics and one named acceptance decision-maker. Use synthetic/redacted fixtures before requesting production access.
2. Specify the smallest deterministic implementation. Introduce AI only when text variability justifies it; keep a review/abstention path and budget approval.
3. Estimate compares with actual sample and flags token-dependent unknowns.
4. **Distinct failure test:** Include polling, filters, branching, retries and external API costs; show which numbers are measured versus assumed.
5. Verify outputs independently of a tool’s “success” response. Test permission loss, retries and partial failures relevant to this scope. Record observed results, residual limitations and restore instructions.
6. Obtain customer acceptance and hand over/revoke temporary access. Do not mark a mock test as a production pass.

**Required access/environment:** One redacted workflow export and run sample, with any active testing limited to explicit staging scope. Production belongs in an appropriately authorized customer-owned account and reliable hosting, not a dependency on the owner’s laptop staying awake. For n8n use cases, check P02 before offering hosted/external configuration access.

## Economics and remaining human work
**New customer-price hypothesis:** CAD220–400 for the stated cap; this is not the owner's startup cost, an observed sale or a conversion of earlier USD ideas. The `historical_price_usd_hypothesis` field, where present, preserves the prior unvalidated USD idea; it is not the current quote. Customer willingness to pay this CAD quote is unverified.

**Efficiency change:** Measure retries, polling and branches; prefer fixing waste over migration.

**Time boundaries:** stop unpaid preparation/qualification for this experiment at four owner-hours total, including the proof; do not build eight custom demos for eight requests. Aim for at most a 60–90 minute reusable fictional proof. The proposed paid delivery allowance is at most 4 hours, including testing and handover, followed by 30–60 minutes of defined defect triage. These are workload limits to validate, not promises that unfamiliar integration work fits them. Quote separately or decline before accepting work that does not fit. Do not omit necessary testing to stay inside the cap.

| Scenario, not forecast | Receipt | Fees / refund reserve assumptions | Allocated cash | All owner hours | Contribution before owner labor/tax | Effective hourly contribution |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Favorable direct at lower quote | CAD220 | 5% combined processing, 0% refund reserve | CAD0 | 6.5 | CAD209.00 | CAD32.15 |
| Marketplace stress at lower quote | CAD220 | 20% fee, 5% refund reserve | CAD25 | 9.5 | CAD140.00 | CAD14.74 |

The favorable scenario allocates one proof hour, one acquisition hour and half an hour of support on top of the delivery cap. The stress case allocates 1.5 proof hours, three acquisition hours and one support hour. Include previous failed pitches and shared business-development time in actual results; they can exceed both examples. The fee percentages are sensitivity assumptions, not assertions of any provider's exact rate. A 20% marketplace case is deliberately conservative; verify the actual provider and contract.

At an illustrative CAD30/hour owner-time target, the stress scenario needs about **CAD413.33** in customer price to break even economically. This is a rejection test, not permission to claim a buyer will pay that price. If that floor exceeds the credible quote, narrow the deliverable without weakening acceptance, use a less costly acquisition channel, or decline. Zero customers produces zero receipts and loses the time/cash spent.

**Unavoidable human work:** qualification, proof of skill, access decisions, scope agreement, ambiguous exceptions, independent acceptance, handover, support and payment reconciliation. Do not call the offer passive. Full methodology: [economics](../../../../../../research/ECONOMICS_V2.md).

## Customer acquisition and validation gate
### Buyer and buying trigger
An agency with an actual client, permitted test data and a named delivery owner. A request must actually match **explain which steps are consuming automation credits before changing plans**; broad interest in AI is not enough.

### Positioning and proof
**Landing/profile headline draft:** Explain which steps are consuming automation credits before changing plans.

**Show, rather than claim:** Three volume scenarios reconcile to an observed redacted bill/run sample. Label all examples fictional. Show actual observed test results only after running them. Keep one relevant annotated screenshot or a 45–90 second demo and a one-page scope; no new website, logo, CRM or subscription is required.

**One-call-to-action draft:** “Send a redacted example of the current problem and the result you need. I will confirm whether it fits this fixed scope before proposing paid work.” This is draft copy, not a message sent.

**Response draft for an invited, eligible buyer request:** “Your request mentions [their exact failure]. My proposed deliverable is: explain which steps are consuming automation credits before changing plans. The check I would use is: three volume scenarios reconcile to an observed redacted bill/run sample. I would first verify whether your existing tools can do this natively. The bounded scope excludes [the project exclusions below]. Are you able to share a redacted example and name the person who will accept the result? I would confirm scope, access and a fixed quote before starting.” Remove any implication of prior client results; do not claim unearned certification.

### $0-first acquisition experiment
Manually inspect the official Make Hire Help and n8n Jobs hiring areas for an explicit, eligible request; do not treat For Hire posts as buyers. Use a warm introduction only where genuine.

**Specific discovery phrase:** `Make credits Zapier task usage audit`. Check current date, location restrictions, budget, exact deliverable, reputation/credential requirements and whether hiring is still open. Search results and community categories are lead-discovery starting points, not a vetted live prospect list.

Prepare at most eight high-fit request records in two batches of four. Obtain owner approval before responses or public posts. Use one reusable proof and personalize the problem, not a generic AI pitch. Stop at four unpaid owner-hours, eight eligible attempts or fourteen elapsed calendar days—whichever comes first—and review what happened. A time-box is not a promised time to first revenue. Pause earlier when no eligible request exists; do not purchase exposure merely to fill a quota.

**Secondary channel:** one relevant, permitted public demonstration or a genuine opt-in referral. No unsolicited mass DMs, scraped email lists or automated applications. Upwork is optional only after eligibility and actual Connects costs are checked; its proposal expense is not assumed zero. Do not move marketplace-sourced pre-contract communication or payment off-platform contrary to its rules.

### Funnel, decision and sale
Record source, eligible request, authorized response, meaningful reply, scoped conversation, funded agreement, accepted delivery, collected receipt, refund and total owner time. Count unpaid likes, followers, waitlist entries and quotes separately from customers. With no meaningful replies after the first four qualified attempts, revise one of buyer/offer/proof before using the second batch; do not simply increase posting volume. With replies but no scoped agreement, record the objection. With no paid commitment at the cap, pause this offer instead of building more features. These are spending/workload gates, not statistical proof of market failure.

Do not begin client-specific production work until there is an agreed scope, lawful permissions, a funded milestone or approved payment arrangement and acceptance criteria. A small paid diagnosis can precede a repair; do not relabel free discovery as a paid deliverable. Ask for a case study or referral only after a real successful delivery and permission.

**Project-specific rejection:** No guaranteed savings without a representative baseline and no quality-reducing shortcut.

### Advertising decision
**Current ad allocation: CAD0.** This narrow service needs proof and qualified conversations before broad paid traffic. Advertised job budgets do not establish conversion economics. Only reassess ads after actual profitable sales; any later test must have a measured conversion path, a conservative acquisition-cost ceiling and a separate approved total budget. No retargeting pixels, uploaded customer lists or campaign launch is authorized by this plan.

**Launch gate:** `buyer_test_only`. For skill-gated work, produce a convincing disposable-environment acceptance test before offering the service. For follow-ons, do not advertise before the earlier project actually has paying clients. # AWA-103 — Monthly single-workflow health review

## Decision and evidence
**Classification:** standalone_service. **Priority:** P3. **Commercial state:** unvalidated. A separately commissioned deliverable is plausible, but it is one offer within a service business, not proof of an independent market.

At least one comparable buyer request was found. That request is not an agreement with this user and may involve a different scope, budget or level of experience. Priority is editorial sequencing for fast, low-upfront-cost experimentation, not probability of success. No workflow implementation, client interview, proposal, contract, paid order or production test was performed for this candidate in this package.

## Buyer, trigger and reason to pay
**Buyer:** Agency with one production integration and clear owner.

**Problem/outcome:** Monthly exception review and short remediation report.

**Buying trigger:** An existing paying client wants an explicit review or small support allowance after a successful delivery.

A defensible fee is for resolving the buyer’s specific mapping/operating problem, measured acceptance, failure handling and usable handover—not for owning a template or merely using AI. Ask for one real failure example and the operational consequence. If native configuration or vendor support solves it adequately, use that cheaper route or decline the custom build.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Native alerts, vendor support and the original implementation warranty may already meet the need.

## Bounded deliverable
Read owner-authorized run history, classify errors, inspect cost and publish review notes.

**Pilot cap:** One known stable workflow, one monthly written review and capped labor.

Include a versioned field/rule map, sanitized export where permitted, test results, known limitations, rollback/recovery instructions and customer-owned handover. Changes outside the cap need a new estimate. No external publication, unsolicited messaging, payments/refunds, destructive data changes or account-wide permissions are implied.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence
1. Confirm the current behavior, ownership, destination semantics and one named acceptance decision-maker. Use synthetic/redacted fixtures before requesting production access.
2. Specify the smallest deterministic implementation. Introduce AI only when text variability justifies it; keep a review/abstention path and budget approval.
3. Deliver one dated report and max two minor fixes within cap.
4. **Distinct failure test:** A green run with empty output is detected by a business-level reconciliation sample; no 24/7 promise.
5. Verify outputs independently of a tool’s “success” response. Test permission loss, retries and partial failures relevant to this scope. Record observed results, residual limitations and restore instructions.
6. Obtain customer acceptance and hand over/revoke temporary access. Do not mark a mock test as a production pass.

**Required access/environment:** Read-only authorized run/usage metadata and named incident owner; runtime secrets remain with the customer. Production belongs in an appropriately authorized customer-owned account and reliable hosting, not a dependency on the owner’s laptop staying awake. For n8n use cases, check P02 before offering hosted/external configuration access.

## Economics and remaining human work
**New customer-price hypothesis:** CAD120–220 for the stated cap; this is not the owner's startup cost, an observed sale or a conversion of earlier USD ideas. The `historical_price_usd_hypothesis` field, where present, preserves the prior unvalidated USD idea; it is not the current quote. Customer willingness to pay this CAD quote is unverified.

**Efficiency change:** Offer only after a stable paid pilot; use existing logs, not a new monitoring platform.

**Time boundaries:** stop new unpaid preparation/qualification for this follow-on at one owner-hour total; do not build eight custom demos for eight requests. Aim for at most a 60–90 minute reusable fictional proof. The proposed paid delivery allowance is at most 2 hours, including testing and handover, followed by 30–60 minutes of defined defect triage. These are workload limits to validate, not promises that unfamiliar integration work fits them. Quote separately or decline before accepting work that does not fit. Do not omit necessary testing to stay inside the cap.

| Scenario, not forecast | Receipt | Fees / refund reserve assumptions | Allocated cash | All owner hours | Contribution before owner labor/tax | Effective hourly contribution |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Favorable direct at lower quote | CAD120 | 5% combined processing, 0% refund reserve | CAD0 | 4.5 | CAD114.00 | CAD25.33 |
| Marketplace stress at lower quote | CAD120 | 20% fee, 5% refund reserve | CAD25 | 7.5 | CAD65.00 | CAD8.67 |

The favorable scenario allocates one proof hour, one acquisition hour and half an hour of support on top of the delivery cap. The stress case allocates 1.5 proof hours, three acquisition hours and one support hour. Include previous failed pitches and shared business-development time in actual results; they can exceed both examples. The fee percentages are sensitivity assumptions, not assertions of any provider's exact rate. A 20% marketplace case is deliberately conservative; verify the actual provider and contract.

At an illustrative CAD30/hour owner-time target, the stress scenario needs about **CAD333.33** in customer price to break even economically. This is a rejection test, not permission to claim a buyer will pay that price. If that floor exceeds the credible quote, narrow the deliverable without weakening acceptance, use a less costly acquisition channel, or decline. Zero customers produces zero receipts and loses the time/cash spent.

**Unavoidable human work:** qualification, proof of skill, access decisions, scope agreement, ambiguous exceptions, independent acceptance, handover, support and payment reconciliation. Do not call the offer passive. Full methodology: [economics](../../../../../../research/ECONOMICS_V2.md).

## Customer acquisition and validation gate
### Buyer and buying trigger
An actual prior paying customer with a recorded recurring or follow-on problem. A request must actually match **review the health of a workflow you already delivered, within a fixed allowance**; broad interest in AI is not enough.

### Positioning and proof
**Landing/profile headline draft:** Review the health of a workflow you already delivered, within a fixed allowance.

**Show, rather than claim:** A monthly run/error/cost snapshot and one documented maintenance recommendation. Label all examples fictional. Show actual observed test results only after running them. Keep one relevant annotated screenshot or a 45–90 second demo and a one-page scope; no new website, logo, CRM or subscription is required.

**One-call-to-action draft:** “Send a redacted example of the current problem and the result you need. I will confirm whether it fits this fixed scope before proposing paid work.” This is draft copy, not a message sent.

**Response draft for an invited, eligible buyer request:** “Your request mentions [their exact failure]. My proposed deliverable is: review the health of a workflow you already delivered, within a fixed allowance. The check I would use is: a monthly run/error/cost snapshot and one documented maintenance recommendation. I would first verify whether your existing tools can do this natively. The bounded scope excludes [the project exclusions below]. Are you able to share a redacted example and name the person who will accept the result? I would confirm scope, access and a fixed quote before starting.” Remove any implication of prior client results; do not claim unearned certification.

### $0-first acquisition experiment
Offer only after the relevant earlier paid delivery or audit, in a consented review discussion; do not run cold ads for this follow-on.

**Specific discovery phrase:** `existing client automation maintenance health check`. Check current date, location restrictions, budget, exact deliverable, reputation/credential requirements and whether hiring is still open. Search results and community categories are lead-discovery starting points, not a vetted live prospect list.

Do not prospect for eight new buyers. Review one actual prior paid client’s documented request, using the existing delivery evidence. Obtain owner approval before making a new commercial offer. Stop after one unpaid scoping hour if the recurring or follow-on need is not clear. A time-box is not a promised time to first revenue. **Secondary channel:** one relevant, permitted public demonstration or a genuine opt-in referral. No unsolicited mass DMs, scraped email lists or automated applications. Do not move marketplace-sourced pre-contract communication or payment off-platform contrary to its rules.

### Funnel, decision and sale
Record source, eligible request, authorized response, meaningful reply, scoped conversation, funded agreement, accepted delivery, collected receipt, refund and total owner time. Count unpaid likes, followers, waitlist entries and quotes separately from customers. If the previous paying customer does not have a current funded need, do not manufacture a retainer or keep following up. With replies but no scoped agreement, record the objection. A small paid diagnosis can precede a repair; do not relabel free discovery as a paid deliverable. Ask for a case study or referral only after a real successful delivery and permission.

**Project-specific rejection:** No unlimited fixes, response SLA or assumed automatic renewal; acquisition is still allocated.

### Advertising decision
**Current ad allocation: CAD0.** This narrow service needs proof and qualified conversations before broad paid traffic. Advertised job budgets do not establish conversion economics. Only reassess ads after actual profitable sales; any later test must have a measured conversion path, a conservative acquisition-cost ceiling and a separate approved total budget. No retargeting pixels, uploaded customer lists or campaign launch is authorized by this plan.

**Launch gate:** `prior_paid_client_required`. For skill-gated work, produce a convincing disposable-environment acceptance test before offering the service. ## Decision and evidence
**Classification:** deferred_download. **Priority:** DEFER. **Commercial state:** unvalidated. This remains a future research option; a downloadable kit or SaaS requires acquisition, maintenance and support evidence not obtained here.

Ask for one real failure example and the operational consequence. If native configuration or vendor support solves it adequately, use that cheaper route or decline the custom build.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Free templates, generated code, built-in test data and platform documentation are strong alternatives.

Generate anonymized tests for same email, household, company switch and shared phone.

**Pilot cap:** Synthetic identity edge cases with human-review labels; no real contact dataset.

Include a versioned field/rule map, sanitized export where permitted, test results, known limitations, rollback/recovery instructions and customer-owned handover. Changes outside the cap need a new estimate. No external publication, unsolicited messaging, payments/refunds, destructive data changes or account-wide permissions are implied.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence
1. Confirm the current behavior, ownership, destination semantics and one named acceptance decision-maker. Use synthetic/redacted fixtures before requesting production access.
2. Specify the smallest deterministic implementation. Introduce AI only when text variability justifies it; keep a review/abstention path and budget approval.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Free templates, generated code, built-in test data and platform documentation are strong alternatives.

Package mock sender, version-bound approval identifiers and audit examples with tests.

**Pilot cap:** One demonstrator approval pattern, mock side effects and version-bound decisions.

# AWA-116 — Schema drift early-warning service

## Decision and evidence
**Classification:** deferred_software. **Priority:** DEFER. **Commercial state:** unvalidated. This remains a future research option; a downloadable kit or SaaS requires acquisition, maintenance and support evidence not obtained here.

The sources establish adjacent work or platform capabilities, not a verified exact-scope buyer for this entry. Validate the particular problem before offering or building it. Priority is editorial sequencing for fast, low-upfront-cost experimentation, not probability of success. No workflow implementation, client interview, proposal, contract, paid order or production test was performed for this candidate in this package.

## Buyer, trigger and reason to pay
**Buyer:** Agency maintaining many client forms and CRM mappings.

**Problem/outcome:** Alerts when incoming field schema differs from approved mapping.

**Buying trigger:** Several paying agencies would need to prove the same unresolved cross-platform problem before this becomes a business case.

A defensible fee is for resolving the buyer’s specific mapping/operating problem, measured acceptance, failure handling and usable handover—not for owning a template or merely using AI. Ask for one real failure example and the operational consequence. If native configuration or vendor support solves it adequately, use that cheaper route or decline the custom build.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Native platform monitoring, replay, mapping tools and established integration products often already meet the need.

## Bounded deliverable
Prototype synthetic webhook schema registry and diff with notification policy.

**Pilot cap:** Synthetic schemas and one explicit compatibility policy.

Include a versioned field/rule map, sanitized export where permitted, test results, known limitations, rollback/recovery instructions and customer-owned handover. Changes outside the cap need a new estimate. No external publication, unsolicited messaging, payments/refunds, destructive data changes or account-wide permissions are implied.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence
1. Confirm the current behavior, ownership, destination semantics and one named acceptance decision-maker. Use synthetic/redacted fixtures before requesting production access.
2. Specify the smallest deterministic implementation. Introduce AI only when text variability justifies it; keep a review/abstention path and budget approval.
3. Demonstrate recurring pain across three paying integrations and quantified savings.
4. **Distinct failure test:** A new optional property and removal of a required field have different severity; no false zero-drift claim on missing samples.
5. Verify outputs independently of a tool’s “success” response. Test permission loss, retries and partial failures relevant to this scope. Record observed results, residual limitations and restore instructions.
6. Obtain customer acceptance and hand over/revoke temporary access. Do not mark a mock test as a production pass.

**Required access/environment:** Local mocks only; no real connectors, external editor access or credential collection before a separately authorized funded design. Production belongs in an appropriately authorized customer-owned account and reliable hosting, not a dependency on the owner’s laptop staying awake. For n8n use cases, check P02 before offering hosted/external configuration access.

## Economics and remaining human work
**Decision: do not build the complete commercial product yet.** Do not build a recurring hosted service until contracts fund operations and expertise. The current CAD0 budget covers a local sample/problem test using existing equipment, not a production software operation. Any prior USD asking price is unvalidated historical context, not expected revenue.

Cap sample/discovery effort at two owner-hours. Reuse previously tested parent assets only when ownership/licensing permits. Do not buy hosting, API credits, a domain, templates or ads. For software, a reliable hosted multi-customer product has unresolved operations/security costs; it is **not** certified to fit CAD100. A download still has transaction fees, support, updates and acquisition work.

Before a build, require specific unmet need and genuine paid evidence, with honest delivery scope and refund terms. A paid implementation that reveals a repeatable need is preferable to promising an unfinished product. Do not collect preorders without separately approved publication/payment terms. Free interest, signups and praise are not payment. Include support and compatibility maintenance in a price-floor calculation; defer when the credible price cannot cover them.

## Customer acquisition and validation gate
**Positioning hypothesis:** A local schema-change detection prototype.

**Free proof, not a speculative catalogue:** Show a synthetic payload change and a non-sensitive difference report. Mark simulated examples and supported versions. Use a static preview already hosted by the existing channel where permitted; no new store/site is needed.

**Primary acquisition:** Ask existing integration clients to supply permitted examples of costly undetected changes. Prepare five genuinely relevant problem discussions/requests; any response or public post needs owner approval. Offer one specific example and ask which missing result they need, rather than pitching “AI automation”. Record exact requested output, existing substitute, willingness to pay and support expectations. For a download, seek two independent actual purchases/paid related implementations before extending the pack. For software, seek three independent paid design partners with a common gap and a funded cost plan before a production build. These are management gates, not probabilities or a claim that presales have happened.

**Draft preview headline:** A local schema-change detection prototype — supported scope, a worked example and clear limits.

**Draft call to action:** “Review the example and tell us which part of your current process it does not solve. A paid version will only be offered after scope, compatibility and delivery terms are clear.” This is not an active listing or waitlist.

## Decision and evidence
**Classification:** deferred_software. **Priority:** DEFER. **Commercial state:** unvalidated. This remains a future research option; a downloadable kit or SaaS requires acquisition, maintenance and support evidence not obtained here.

## Buyer, trigger and reason to pay
**Buyer:** Implementers whose deployment QA is manual and inconsistent.

**Problem/outcome:** A test runner for supported workflow exports with deterministic fixtures.

**Buying trigger:** Several paying agencies would need to prove the same unresolved cross-platform problem before this becomes a business case.

A defensible fee is for resolving the buyer’s specific mapping/operating problem, measured acceptance, failure handling and usable handover—not for owning a template or merely using AI. Ask for one real failure example and the operational consequence. If native configuration or vendor support solves it adequately, use that cheaper route or decline the custom build.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Native platform monitoring, replay, mapping tools and established integration products often already meet the need.

## Bounded deliverable
Build local CLI harness against fake CRM/webhook endpoints and structured assertions.

**Pilot cap:** Local deterministic mock connectors and stable assertions.

Changes outside the cap need a new estimate. No external publication, unsolicited messaging, payments/refunds, destructive data changes or account-wide permissions are implied.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence

6. Obtain customer acceptance and hand over/revoke temporary access. Do not mark a mock test as a production pass.

# AWA-121 — Existing Apps Script trigger recovery

## Decision and evidence
**Classification:** standalone_service. **Priority:** P2. **Commercial state:** unvalidated.
Adjacent request: the retrieved repair job includes Gmail and low advertised hourly rates; this narrower internal-only offer has no exact paid validation. This is a scoped offer within the existing service business, not proof of an independent market. No customer was contacted, charged or served by preparing this plan.

## Buyer, trigger and reason to pay
**Buyer:** An operations owner or agency maintaining an existing internal Google Sheets script.

**Problem/outcome:** A previously useful internal script has stopped firing or creates duplicate output.

**Buying trigger:** A current owner requests a solution to this specific existing problem and can define an accepted result.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Google trigger history, quota/error messages and native sheet functions before any replacement workflow.

## Bounded deliverable
**Pilot cap:** One existing non-email script, one installable trigger and one input/output pair; a 90-minute paid diagnostic with any repair separately scoped. No bulk mail, financial writes or new application.

Include a versioned scope, test result, known limitations and handover. Production changes require separately approved scoped access, customer-owned running costs and acceptance criteria. No new owner-funded infrastructure.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence
1. Confirm a permitted example of the failure and the buyer's authority. Reject missing consent or data rights.
2. Prefer native configuration, deterministic rules and existing approved tools.
3. A fictional input sheet, an intentionally disabled trigger and a duplicate-event case, with a documented recovery decision.
4. **Distinct failure test:** A trigger executes twice or loses authorization; output cannot silently duplicate and the owner receives an explicit diagnostic.
5. Record expected and observed results; false confidence is a failed acceptance test.
6. Obtain customer acceptance of a funded scoped job and revoke temporary access. Synthetic tests are not production acceptance.

## Economics and remaining human work
**New customer-price hypothesis:** CAD150–280 for the stated cap; this is not the owner's startup cost, an observed sale or a conversion of earlier USD ideas. The `historical_price_usd_hypothesis` field, where present, preserves the prior unvalidated USD idea; it is not the current quote. Customer willingness to pay this CAD quote is unverified.

**Efficiency change:** Inspect the existing code and execution log; reuse its working logic and stop diagnosis at 90 minutes.

**Time boundaries:** stop unpaid preparation/qualification for this experiment at four owner-hours total, including the proof; do not build eight custom demos for eight requests. Aim for at most a 60–90 minute reusable fictional proof. The proposed paid delivery allowance is at most 2 hours, including testing and handover, followed by 30–60 minutes of defined defect triage. These are workload limits to validate, not promises that unfamiliar integration work fits them. Quote separately or decline before accepting work that does not fit. Do not omit necessary testing to stay inside the cap.

| Scenario, not forecast | Receipt | Fees / refund reserve assumptions | Allocated cash | All owner hours | Contribution before owner labor/tax | Effective hourly contribution |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Favorable direct at lower quote | CAD150 | 5% combined processing, 0% refund reserve | CAD0 | 4.5 | CAD142.50 | CAD31.67 |
| Marketplace stress at lower quote | CAD150 | 20% fee, 5% refund reserve | CAD25 | 7.5 | CAD87.50 | CAD11.67 |

The favorable scenario allocates one proof hour, one acquisition hour and half an hour of support on top of the delivery cap. The stress case allocates 1.5 proof hours, three acquisition hours and one support hour. Include previous failed pitches and shared business-development time in actual results; they can exceed both examples. The fee percentages are sensitivity assumptions, not assertions of any provider's exact rate. A 20% marketplace case is deliberately conservative; verify the actual provider and contract.

At an illustrative CAD30/hour owner-time target, the stress scenario needs about **CAD333.33** in customer price to break even economically. This is a rejection test, not permission to claim a buyer will pay that price. If that floor exceeds the credible quote, narrow the deliverable without weakening acceptance, use a less costly acquisition channel, or decline. Zero customers produces zero receipts and loses the time/cash spent.

**Unavoidable human work:** qualification, proof of skill, access decisions, scope agreement, ambiguous exceptions, independent acceptance, handover, support and payment reconciliation. Do not call the offer passive. Full methodology: [economics](../../../../../../research/ECONOMICS_V2.md).

## Customer acquisition and validation gate
### Buyer and buying trigger
An operations owner with an existing repetitive process, a sample and an approved definition of correct output. A request must actually match **find why an existing internal sheets script stopped running**; broad interest in AI is not enough.

### Positioning and proof
**Landing/profile headline draft:** Find why an existing internal Sheets script stopped running.

**Show, rather than claim:** A reproduction and trigger/authorization/duplicate-output checklist, not an unbounded code rewrite. Label all examples fictional. Show actual observed test results only after running them. Keep one relevant annotated screenshot or a 45–90 second demo and a one-page scope; no new website, logo, CRM or subscription is required.

**One-call-to-action draft:** “Send a redacted example of the current problem and the result you need. I will confirm whether it fits this fixed scope before proposing paid work.” This is draft copy, not a message sent.

**Response draft for an invited, eligible buyer request:** “Your request mentions [their exact failure]. My proposed deliverable is: find why an existing internal sheets script stopped running. The check I would use is: a reproduction and trigger/authorization/duplicate-output checklist, not an unbounded code rewrite. I would first verify whether your existing tools can do this natively. The bounded scope excludes [the project exclusions below]. Are you able to share a redacted example and name the person who will accept the result? I would confirm scope, access and a fixed quote before starting.” Remove any implication of prior client results; do not claim unearned certification.

### $0-first acquisition experiment
Use explicit spreadsheet/workflow implementation requests and opt-in agency referrals. Prepare a short local proof before considering any paid marketplace proposal.

**Specific discovery phrase:** `Google Apps Script existing trigger stopped duplicate`. Check current date, location restrictions, budget, exact deliverable, reputation/credential requirements and whether hiring is still open. Search results and community categories are lead-discovery starting points, not a vetted live prospect list.

Prepare at most eight high-fit request records in two batches of four. Obtain owner approval before responses or public posts. # AWA-126 — Measured credit-reduction retrofit for an existing workflow

## Decision and evidence
**Classification:** standalone_service. **Priority:** P2. **Commercial state:** unvalidated.
Technical cost constraints and staged implementation requests support testing this follow-on; no exact paying customer or guaranteed saving has been verified. This is a scoped offer within the existing service business, not proof of an independent market. No customer was contacted, charged or served by preparing this plan.

## Buyer, trigger and reason to pay
**Buyer:** A prior AWA-095 audit customer with a specific measured source of unnecessary automation work.

**Problem/outcome:** Polling, repeated processing or an unnecessary branch uses avoidable credits without adding a required output.

**Buying trigger:** A current owner requests a solution to this specific existing problem and can define an accepted result.

**Native/free/AI alternatives:** Native scheduling/filter settings and plan configuration first; do not rebuild a flow that is already efficient.

## Bounded deliverable
**Pilot cap:** One audited workflow, one agreed optimization, identical acceptance fixtures and a before/after usage comparison. No migration, reduced validation, removed error reporting or promises about future provider prices.

Include a versioned scope, test result, known limitations and handover. Production changes require separately approved scoped access, customer-owned running costs and acceptance criteria. No new owner-funded infrastructure.

## Acceptance and implementation sequence
1. Confirm a permitted example of the failure and the buyer's authority. Reject missing consent or data rights.
2. Prefer native configuration, deterministic rules and existing approved tools.
3. A fixed sample is run against baseline and proposed logic; output parity and total credits, including retries, are compared.
4. **Distinct failure test:** Any output mismatch, missing alert or rise in error rate fails the retrofit even if the credit total falls.
5. Record expected and observed results; false confidence is a failed acceptance test.
6. Obtain customer acceptance of a funded scoped job and revoke temporary access. Synthetic tests are not production acceptance.

## Economics and remaining human work
**New customer-price hypothesis:** CAD300–600 for the stated cap; this is not the owner's startup cost, an observed sale or a conversion of earlier USD ideas. The `historical_price_usd_hypothesis` field, where present, preserves the prior unvalidated USD idea; it is not the current quote. Customer willingness to pay this CAD quote is unverified.

**Efficiency change:** Only implement the one change identified by the paid audit; preserve error handling and approval gates.

**Time boundaries:** stop new unpaid preparation/qualification for this follow-on at one owner-hour total; do not build eight custom demos for eight requests. Aim for at most a 60–90 minute reusable fictional proof. The proposed paid delivery allowance is at most 6 hours, including testing and handover, followed by 30–60 minutes of defined defect triage. These are workload limits to validate, not promises that unfamiliar integration work fits them. Quote separately or decline before accepting work that does not fit. Do not omit necessary testing to stay inside the cap.

| Scenario, not forecast | Receipt | Fees / refund reserve assumptions | Allocated cash | All owner hours | Contribution before owner labor/tax | Effective hourly contribution |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Favorable direct at lower quote | CAD300 | 5% combined processing, 0% refund reserve | CAD0 | 8.5 | CAD285.00 | CAD33.53 |
| Marketplace stress at lower quote | CAD300 | 20% fee, 5% refund reserve | CAD25 | 11.5 | CAD200.00 | CAD17.39 |

The favorable scenario allocates one proof hour, one acquisition hour and half an hour of support on top of the delivery cap. The stress case allocates 1.5 proof hours, three acquisition hours and one support hour. Include previous failed pitches and shared business-development time in actual results; they can exceed both examples. The fee percentages are sensitivity assumptions, not assertions of any provider's exact rate. A 20% marketplace case is deliberately conservative; verify the actual provider and contract.

At an illustrative CAD30/hour owner-time target, the stress scenario needs about **CAD493.33** in customer price to break even economically. This is a rejection test, not permission to claim a buyer will pay that price. If that floor exceeds the credible quote, narrow the deliverable without weakening acceptance, use a less costly acquisition channel, or decline. Zero customers produces zero receipts and loses the time/cash spent.

**Unavoidable human work:** qualification, proof of skill, access decisions, scope agreement, ambiguous exceptions, independent acceptance, handover, support and payment reconciliation. Do not call the offer passive. Full methodology: [economics](../../../../../../../research/ECONOMICS_V2.md).

## Customer acquisition and validation gate
### Buyer and buying trigger
An actual prior paying customer with a recorded recurring or follow-on problem. A request must actually match **remove one measured source of wasted credits without removing safeguards**; broad interest in AI is not enough.

### Positioning and proof
**Landing/profile headline draft:** Remove one measured source of wasted credits without removing safeguards.

**Show, rather than claim:** An output-parity report beside observed before/after credit use and rollback instructions. Label all examples fictional. Show actual observed test results only after running them. Keep one relevant annotated screenshot or a 45–90 second demo and a one-page scope; no new website, logo, CRM or subscription is required.

**One-call-to-action draft:** “Send a redacted example of the current problem and the result you need. I will confirm whether it fits this fixed scope before proposing paid work.” This is draft copy, not a message sent.

**Response draft for an invited, eligible buyer request:** “Your request mentions [their exact failure]. My proposed deliverable is: remove one measured source of wasted credits without removing safeguards. The check I would use is: an output-parity report beside observed before/after credit use and rollback instructions. I would first verify whether your existing tools can do this natively. The bounded scope excludes [the project exclusions below]. Are you able to share a redacted example and name the person who will accept the result? I would confirm scope, access and a fixed quote before starting.” Remove any implication of prior client results; do not claim unearned certification.

### $0-first acquisition experiment
Offer only after the relevant earlier paid delivery or audit, in a consented review discussion; do not run cold ads for this follow-on.

**Specific discovery phrase:** `existing audit customer Make credits polling reduction`. Check current date, location restrictions, budget, exact deliverable, reputation/credential requirements and whether hiring is still open. Search results and community categories are lead-discovery starting points, not a vetted live prospect list.

Do not prospect for eight new buyers. Review one actual prior paid client’s documented request, using the existing delivery evidence. Obtain owner approval before making a new commercial offer. Stop after one unpaid scoping hour if the recurring or follow-on need is not clear. A time-box is not a promised time to first revenue. Pause earlier when no eligible request exists; do not purchase exposure merely to fill a quota.

**Secondary channel:** one relevant, permitted public demonstration or a genuine opt-in referral. No unsolicited mass DMs, scraped email lists or automated applications. Upwork is optional only after eligibility and actual Connects costs are checked; its proposal expense is not assumed zero. Do not move marketplace-sourced pre-contract communication or payment off-platform contrary to its rules.

### Funnel, decision and sale
Record source, eligible request, authorized response, meaningful reply, scoped conversation, funded agreement, accepted delivery, collected receipt, refund and total owner time. Count unpaid likes, followers, waitlist entries and quotes separately from customers. If the previous paying customer does not have a current funded need, do not manufacture a retainer or keep following up. With replies but no scoped agreement, record the objection. With no paid commitment at the cap, pause this offer instead of building more features. These are spending/workload gates, not statistical proof of market failure.

Do not begin client-specific production work until there is an agreed scope, lawful permissions, a funded milestone or approved payment arrangement and acceptance criteria. A small paid diagnosis can precede a repair; do not relabel free discovery as a paid deliverable. Ask for a case study or referral only after a real successful delivery and permission.

**Project-specific rejection:** No sale before a representative baseline and a customer-confirmed payback case; this is an AWA-095 follow-on, not another independent market.

### Advertising decision
**Current ad allocation: CAD0.** This narrow service needs proof and qualified conversations before broad paid traffic. Advertised job budgets do not establish conversion economics. Only reassess ads after actual profitable sales; any later test must have a measured conversion path, a conservative acquisition-cost ceiling and a separate approved total budget. No retargeting pixels, uploaded customer lists or campaign launch is authorized by this plan.

**Launch gate:** `prior_paid_client_required`. For skill-gated work, produce a convincing disposable-environment acceptance test before offering the service. For follow-ons, do not advertise before the earlier project actually has paying clients. [Marketing method](../../../../../../../research/MARKETING_PLAYBOOK.md) · [Validation gates](../../../../../../../research/VALIDATION_GATES.md).

No paid order, finished implementation, live test or recurring revenue is recorded. Next action is the current frontmatter next_action; append observed actions without resetting this checkpoint.

## Evidence references

- [V2-07](https://help.make.com/credits) — Make credit accounting. indexed_primary; Measure the proposed flow at realistic volume; a platform plan does not cover every external provider.

Supports testing bounded discovery rather than selling unlimited rescue.

Absolute project ceiling: CAD100, not a target.** The ceiling includes tax, FX cost, committed renewals, proposal credits, demonstrations and advertising through the first-sale/first-30-day experiment. documents.body:
# Business Portfolio — revision 2
**Research-informed plans and a local project explorer · November 5, 2026**

**Double-click [Open_Project_Browser.cmd](Open_Project_Browser.cmd) for the live project explorer.** It starts or reuses the read-only local service. Changes to canonical Markdown appear within a few seconds. The [static snapshot](PROJECT_BROWSER.html) remains available offline, clearly labelled as a snapshot. The complete ZIP retains individual Markdown files and rebuild tools. No customer workflow, advertisement, account or payment executes from the browser.

## What is in this revision
**139 resumable records:** 56 scoped service candidates (including one explicit audit follow-on), 58 bundled components, six deferred downloads, six deferred software ideas, 12 existing-work records and one integration record. All 133 prior IDs/progress records are retained; AWA-121 through AWA-126 are new. These are not 139 independent businesses or validated income sources.

Each applicable record has a buyer-specific outcome, proof asset, native-first delivery shortcut, acquisition route/draft, effort boundary, budget gate, measurement/stop rule and honest economic sensitivity. Bundle/internal records explicitly do not need independent advertising. Existing product records contain specific launch/promotion drafts without changing their approved releases.

**Budget:** CAD0 preferred, CAD100 absolute cumulative owner-launch ceiling per selected project, no automatic reset. Current authorized spend is CAD0 portfolio-wide. Proposed service prices are separate from startup costs. Production costs must be identified and accepted by the customer; free prototypes do not establish affordable production. Six software candidates remain discovery-only.

**Evidence:** 108 source records, including 41 additional policy/technical/competitor/channel/buyer/repository records reviewed for this revision. The other 67 are carried forward, not newly reverified. No new paid order or measured success probability is claimed.

## Start with the evidence and a small test
[Research findings](research/RESEARCH_V2.md) · [Priorities](research/PRIORITIES_V2.md) · [Marketing and advertising](research/MARKETING_PLAYBOOK.md) · [Budget policy](research/BUDGET_POLICY.md) · [Economics](research/ECONOMICS_V2.md) · [Validation gates](research/VALIDATION_GATES.md) · [New sources](research/SOURCES_V2.md).

An eligible requested problem, scoped skill proof and buyer-funded delivery are stronger starting points than a generic “AI agent” catalogue. Consider AWA-005, AWA-001, AWA-007 or AWA-012; AWA-122 is a narrower new document-assembly option. Choose one primary and at most one related fallback. Existing EX-001/EX-002 promotions should reuse assets, not restart product development.

## Existing work is preserved
Published calculator/inventory records retain their reported status and unknown paid demand. Storefront, prototype, supplier reality-check, current Computer Bridge and legacy tools remain traceable. No local Windows, native Excel, private order or live-store re-verification was performed here. Checkmarks keep their original evidence basis; no fictional progress percentage or revenue is added.

## Install or merge safely
Read [REPO_PLACEMENT.md](REPO_PLACEMENT.md). The ZIP contains the outer `business_portfolio/` directory. If no local folder exists, extract into the repository root. If a prior package or newer local changes exist, **stage outside the checkout and merge by ID** using [CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_PROMPT.md](CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_PROMPT.md). Never overwrite newer local progress.

```powershell
python business_portfolio/tools/build_browser.py
python business_portfolio/tools/build_browser.py --check
python -m unittest discover -s business_portfolio/tests -v
python business_portfolio/tools/commercial_checks.py --portfolio business_portfolio
```

The tools require Python 3.10+ and only its standard library. They validate local records and arithmetic; they do not spend, enforce bank/provider limits, contact prospects or operate the bridge. The optional developer browser QA uses a separately available Playwright environment; no browser-test dependency is needed to browse/rebuild this package.

Read [QA_REPORT.md](QA_REPORT.md) for checks actually run and remaining acceptance limitations. Source Markdown is canonical; the HTML/JSON are generated. Keep all credentials, customer documents, real leads, orders, consent evidence and financial ledgers outside the public repository.

## Local integration and live view

Read [INTEGRATION_STATUS.md](INTEGRATION_STATUS.md) for current local tests, state preservation and limits. The supplied MANIFEST.json, CHECKSUMS.sha256 and QA_REPORT.md are historical delivery-snapshot evidence after local edits; they are not claims that edited files still match the ZIP. LOCAL_MANIFEST.json records the edited local snapshot separately.

The service listens only on http://127.0.0.1:22841 and uses the Python standard library. It serves validated portfolio data plus explicitly listed source guides and public product links. It never serves arbitrary paths, private releases, customer records or a filesystem browser. There is no account, scheduler, AI engine or spending capability. No dependencies were installed.

Each intentional launcher run opens or requests reuse of the browser page while reusing the running service. The default browser may create another tab; reliable tab detection is not available, so the launcher does not suppress reopening. The service stops at Windows sign-out/restart; the next launcher run starts it again. Temporary incomplete/invalid edits keep the last valid view and display a warning. A developer can run `python business_portfolio/tools/serve_browser.py` in a console and use Ctrl+C to stop it.

Files & Results labels source guides separately from actual delivery assets. Paid customer archives and the private demo stay protected; no containing-folder OS command is exposed through HTTP. Additional deliverables need a specific safe entry in the service guide registry, not a broad folder permission.

Declared non-sensitive text results can appear automatically; see [the public-results format](SCHEMA.md). The service does not guess at paid releases, private videos or complete build folders. Those remain explicitly withheld or unverified.

Startup failures keep the CMD window open with an error. Background service startup output is written to the ignored `.local/browser-startup.log` when available. The visible Python launcher checks service health before requesting the page; it no longer hides all failures behind pythonw.

documents.title: Further research: selection, acquisition and budget fit
documents.body:
# Further research: selection, acquisition and budget fit
Reviewed 2026-11-05 · 41 additional source records · no customer contact or paid validation

## Decision
The most defensible first test is still a small implementation or diagnostic for a buyer with an existing system and a specific current problem. Prefer fixing a missing mapping, diagnosing one failed webhook, or delivering one form-to-CRM path over a vague “AI agent”, content factory or multi-tenant SaaS. This is an editorial conclusion from buyer-request specificity, tool competition and cost/effort constraints—not a measured probability of success.

The priority is not to build more before selling. Qualify a real request, reuse one small proof, quote a bounded result and measure the all-in economics. Keep multiple options available, but run at most one primary and one related fallback acquisition experiment at a time. Owner time can be expensive even when cash spending is zero.

## What changed in the evidence
**Agency implementation is real stated demand, but not an assured opportunity.** A newly reviewed indexed marketing-agency request asks for customer-owned n8n/Make setups, cost estimates, checking and handover (V2-29). Another operations request separates assessment from implementation (V2-32). These support narrow delivery and paid diagnostics; neither establishes this owner's win rate or earnings.

**Low headline budgets are often traps for this goal.** Retrieved examples include US$100 for AI lead qualification, US$50 for broad social-content automation and US$200 across four US$50 guides (V2-30/V2-31/V2-40). Broad fixed-price commitments can fail the workload model. The revision does not copy those budgets into profitable forecasts.

**Higher asking budgets are not automatically accessible.** One tracking listing is US-only (V2-37). A MailerLite job requires established expert marketplace credentials (V2-38). A strategic automation request shows substantial competition and experience expectations (V2-39). These are filtered out unless eligibility and competence are actually met. Job status, applicant counts and advertised prices are snapshots, not confirmed current vacancies, contract values or payment records.

**Existing-stack document work is worth a bounded test.** A Sheets/Docs reporting request advertises US$500 for a broader setup (V2-33). AWA-122 narrows this to one approved template, deterministic substitutions and manual review, with no sensitive assessments or reporting-model redesign. This is an adjacent demand signal, not evidence someone has bought that exact smaller offer.

**Technical funnel setup is not “ensure it sells.”** A Payhip/email/author-site request supports adjacent demand for setup help (V2-34), but includes more work than checkout QA. New AWA-123 and AWA-124 explicitly sell a checked delivery path or consent-based native sequence—not guaranteed traffic, deliverability or revenue. Tracking AWA-125 stays skill-gated and does not imply an analytics event proves incremental sales.

## Free/native competition and costs
Make has a limited free-credit allowance; Apps Script has quotas; MailerLite's current free plan is limited to 250 subscribers and 2,500 emails per month (V2-06/V2-12/V2-14). A required premium feature or provider usage charge cannot be ignored to advertise a CAD0 setup. Customer-owned platforms are the default production path, after checking exact feature, volume and cost requirements.

Use native Shopify Flow when adequate instead of adding a new automation subscription; an existing eligible paid Shopify plan is still required and some actions are plan-gated (V2-15). Use the existing CRM connector, ESP automation, project template or vendor report where it solves the problem. The value is a well-scoped correct outcome and supportable handover, not merely using AI.

The old n8n licence URL did not resolve during this review. The current repository documentation was used instead (V2-11); the former URL's failure is recorded rather than silently treating it as read. Consulting and unrestricted hosted-product rights are not interchangeable. Keep production licence review as a gate.

## Selling the existing downloads
Payhip's free subscription still has transaction and payment-processing costs (V2-01). Its marketplace has a genuine-sale eligibility threshold and review (V2-02); do not assume it supplies the first customer. Free Jobber cleaning templates and Smartsheet inventory templates are real alternatives (V2-24/V2-25). The revised existing-product records include honest positioning, reusable demonstration assets, permitted organic distribution, funnel metrics and stop rules.

Low-price downloadable products have little room for paid acquisition when support and fees are included. The shared model shows the break-even arithmetic using explicitly hypothetical processor/refund/support inputs, rather than claiming current ad prices or conversion. Ads are in the launch plans as a conditional later experiment, not an automatic expense.

## Sources and limits
There are 108 source records in this revision: 67 inherited and 41 added/rechecked records. This is not a claim of 108 newly inspected independent markets or pages. New records identify full-page, indexed-primary and connector access. Several Upwork pages blocked direct retrieval; indexed text is useful for cautious stated-demand examples, but precise live eligibility and scope must be rechecked before applying. 12 added records are buyer-request examples, two are channel pages, and the rest include technical/policy/competitor/repository context; categories can describe adjacent—not exact—demand.

No interviews, proposals, payment transactions, production tests or advertisement experiments were performed. No sales probability, conversion rate, monthly income or passivity claim has been verified. “Buyer-test-only” means research merits a cheap test; it does not mean ready-to-launch, funded or commercially validated. [New source register](SOURCES_V2.md) · [Marketing](MARKETING_PLAYBOOK.md) · [Budget](BUDGET_POLICY.md).
