documents.body:
# What to try first—and what not to start
No ranking is a probability of success. All exact offers remain unvalidated.

## Primary options
| Priority | Project | Why consider it | Condition before offering |
|---|---|---|---|
| First small diagnostic/repair | AWA-005 — form field mapping rescue | Specific visible failure, limited fields, existing tools | Reproduce a permitted example and validate skill; no full rebuild |
| First bounded implementation | AWA-001 — form-to-CRM starter | Comparable implementation requests; concrete result | Customer owns the stack, native alternative inadequate, scoped quote covers all time |
| Alternative diagnostic | AWA-007 — broken webhook diagnostic | Sell an investigation before accepting unknown repair work | Buyer understands that diagnosis, not a guaranteed fix, is purchased |
| Existing-work takeover | AWA-012 — unfinished workflow assessment | Avoids an unlimited rescue promise | Read-only access and named acceptance owner; no fixed-price full completion before assessment |
| New adjacent test | AWA-122 — approved Sheets-to-Docs report assembly | Relevant request signal, deterministic output and existing tools | Template is complete, no regulated assessment, quota/layout cases demonstrated |
| Existing-asset sales test | EX-001 / EX-002 | Products and store already exist; no new build needed | Truthful compatibility/free-alternative comparison and a permission-appropriate channel |

Run one service test and optionally one small existing-product promotion test, not all six at once. Stop each at its own work/cash gate; the portfolio still retains the broad long-term options. The product test may produce no income; zero setup cash does not imply strong demand.

## Six additional candidates
AWA-121 internal Apps Script trigger diagnosis; AWA-122 approved document assembly; AWA-123 digital-download delivery QA; AWA-124 opt-in welcome/suppression setup; AWA-125 one purchase-event acceptance test; AWA-126 one measured credit-reduction retrofit.

These are six additional scoped service offers, not six validated businesses. AWA-126 is an explicit follow-on to AWA-095; do not count its client as a second independent market. AWA-125 needs demonstrable analytics/consent competence and is not a first-sales recommendation. AWA-121's related job has low advertised rates, so a sensible quote still needs buyer proof. AWA-123/124 are adjacent to a broader funnel request, not directly proven standalone purchases.

## Defer or reject for this objective
Generic AI-content machines with large scope and low budgets; broad CRM rescues priced before diagnosis; migrations justified only by a cheap advertised plan; owner-hosted client production; 24/7 retainers; security/compliance certifications; production token-vault or multi-tenant software under an assumed CAD100 total cost; broad paid ads for the CA$9/CA$15 products before conversion economics exist; purchased lists or unsolicited automated outreach.

The 58 components remain parent deliverables, not independent products. The 12 download/software candidates stay demand-gated. Existing tools and archives remain preserved, not commercialized by default. A proposed customer price is accepted only when a real buyer agrees and the measured work fits—not because the spreadsheet says it should.

documents.title: Marketing is part of the project—not an afterthought
documents.body:
# Marketing is part of the project—not an afterthought
Revision 2 · draft activities only · CAD0-first

## The acquisition sequence
Select one primary offer and at most one related fallback test, not 56 simultaneous launches. Keep the broad portfolio for later choice. A small work-in-progress limit prevents paying for many unproven funnels while preserving the user's larger portfolio goal.

1. Identify an actual buyer and buying event. Record the current workaround, costly failure, native/free alternative and acceptance owner.
2. Define one result and an explicit exclusion list. Use a 60–90 minute reusable fictional proof, not free custom production work. Do not claim experience or results the owner does not have.
3. Prepare a compact sales asset: one outcome headline, relevant screenshot/test, scope, customer tool requirements, limitations, test-price hypothesis and one call to action. An existing profile, allowed community post or existing Payhip listing is enough; no new website is required.
4. Reach the buyer through a permission-appropriate channel. Use the project-specific discovery phrase and channel, not a generic “we automate everything” campaign.
5. Ask for a redacted example and scope agreement; use a funded bounded milestone or approved arrangement before client-specific implementation.
6. Measure all time/costs, collected payments, acceptance, refunds and support. Use real customer permission for a testimonial or case study, then assess repeatable delivery.

These are sequential gates, not a guarantee of sales. The first unpaid-work limit is deliberately small. When evidence is weak, pausing saves time; writing more code does not establish demand.

## Service channels and scripts
**Primary no-cash discovery:** manually review explicit hiring requests in the official Make Hire Help area or n8n Jobs, separating buyers from sellers and respecting category rules. Platform membership is not partner accreditation. Current availability, eligibility, price, security and scope must be checked for each request. [Make hiring](https://community.make.com/c/hire-a-pro/hire-help/74) · [Make posting rules](https://community.make.com/t/looking-to-hire-an-expert-or-offer-your-services-hire-a-pro-is-the-right-space/96837) · [n8n jobs](https://community.n8n.io/c/jobs/13).

**Secondary:** a genuine warm referral or one permitted public demonstration. There is no assumed existing audience or referral network. If neither an eligible request nor permission-appropriate channel exists, the free route has not been established; pause rather than label customer acquisition solved.

**Optional paid acquisition:** a few individually selected Upwork proposals only after checking Connects and actual contract fees, geography, credentials and available cash. Never scrape/apply automatically or create fake work history. No bidding credits are purchased by this request. A new Fiverr profile is not a default infrastructure task and has no guaranteed discovery.

Each service record includes a project-specific draft response. Use the buyer's actual problem and a relevant acceptance test, not a mass-generated opener. A suitable message asks for the missing scoped information and does not claim a fictional sample is past client work. Follow marketplace communication/payment rules.

Use two batches of at most four eligible requests, with a maximum four total unpaid owner-hours or fourteen elapsed days. Four silent attempts are a reason to inspect targeting/proof, not a statistically valid declaration of no demand. Spend the second batch only after a useful adjustment; at the cap, pause and record the result. A buyer conversation, signed scope, funded milestone and collected money are distinct stages.

## Digital products: the complete small launch
Use EX-001 and EX-002's specific copy/asset plans. Before a new download is sold, its project must contain: buyer problem, native/free substitutes, supported environment, honest worked example, finished deliverable inventory, licence/refund/support terms, accepted payment method, a tested permitted delivery path, distribution route and a measurement plan. Do not list an unfinished product as immediately deliverable.

A useful free sample should demonstrate a specific paid benefit; it is not evidence of willingness to pay. Existing low-price products already have releases: reuse those and do not restart authoring or storefront setup. The first test is one or two permission-appropriate placements with source tracking, not a daily-content job for weeks.

Product copy should answer “why this instead of the free alternative?” through an observable difference. Do not invent a bundle discount, claimed original price, bestseller status, review count, guaranteed savings or limited stock. Paid templates face free/native/AI competition; honesty about compatibility can reduce conversions but is still necessary.

## Advertising included, but gated
Advertising is not automatically efficient. Current ads allocation is CAD0. Paid traffic can be considered only after genuine sales and measured contribution show room for acquisition cost. Three independent paid orders and a measured funnel are a minimal management checkpoint for considering a tiny learning test, not statistical proof of profitable scaling. Do not infer cold-traffic conversion from friends/referrals or manufacture purchases to pass a gate.

For a later approved test, use **one offer, one audience and one conversion action**, with a written hypothesis and an all-in maximum CAD25 initial spend. Prefer exact problem intent over broad “AI” interests. Draft two honest headlines from the project's outcome and one proof-based description. Examples: “Fix missing CRM form fields” / “One field map. A checked result.”; for downloads, reuse the existing product headline, not a claim of guaranteed profit. Research keyword availability and eligibility before any ad purchase; this package does not estimate current click prices.

Record the expected audience, destination, exact claim, approved creative, conversion action, source tag, attribution caveats, spend ceiling, time boundary and stop condition. Reject the test if required minimum budgets, tracking, lawful consent or billing controls do not fit. Do not install pixels or upload customer lists without separate permission. Google average daily budgets are not hard total caps; verify current controls or do not launch. [Budget rules](BUDGET_POLICY.md).

Stop immediately on a broken destination, wrong price, tracking failure, misleading claim, consent issue or capped spend. Do not automatically increase budget after clicks or one sale. Continue only when the small test produces a credible signal worth a separately approved follow-up; CAD25 is not enough to claim broad statistical certainty. No spend/creative optimization runs unattended here.

## Email, affiliates, SEO and repeat business
Use genuine opt-in email only, with appropriate sender identity and unsubscribe behavior. Social DMs can be commercial electronic messages; “B2B” or a publicly displayed address does not automatically authorize outreach. Consult the CRTC guidance and get appropriate advice for uncertainty. Do not use a consent-request email as a loophole to blast strangers. [CRTC FAQ](https://crtc.gc.ca/eng/com500/faq500.htm).

Affiliates may be a later revenue-share channel, not free guaranteed distribution. Require an actual willing partner, disclosed connection, a commission that fits contribution, accurate claims, clear payout/refund handling and permission. Payhip's seller-managed payouts add work. No affiliate is recruited or paid by this plan. [Payhip affiliate help](https://help.payhip.com/article/95-affiliates) · [Competition Bureau](https://competition-bureau.canada.ca/en/deceptive-marketing-practices/types-deceptive-marketing-practices/influencer-marketing-and-competition-act).

SEO and content can compound but are not assumed fast first income. Write one useful answer/example for a verified recurring question; avoid mass AI pages, a new blog infrastructure project or an unmeasured publication treadmill. Existing satisfied customers are a sensible place to ask about a genuinely recurring problem; offer a maintenance scope only after that need exists. A subscription is not passive without measured exception/support labor.

## Metrics and interpretation
Track eligible requests → approved responses/placements → qualified visits/replies → scoped conversations/checkout starts → funded/paid orders → accepted delivery → refunds/repeat orders. Deduplicate channels and exclude synthetic/free/self test orders from genuine demand. Use aggregate/pseudonymous public notes; keep actual contacts, orders, financial evidence and consent records private. The JSON experiment template contains null outcomes, not fabricated data.

documents.title: CAD100 ceiling, CAD0-first operating policy
documents.body:
# CAD100 ceiling, CAD0-first operating policy
Revision 2 · 2026-11-05 · planning, not spending authorization

## What the limit means
The user's “price for each project” is treated as **incremental owner cash required to validate/start it**, not the price charged to a customer. Because the owner is in Canada, the cap is expressed in CAD. Customer prices may be higher and are separately labeled hypotheses. No foreign-exchange conversion was used to present old USD asking prices as verified CAD prices.

Prefer CAD0. The **absolute ceiling is CAD100** per selected project through its first-sale/first-30-day validation experiment. Include tax, exchange/conversion charges, proposal credits, trial/API usage, ads, hosting and noncancelable commitments. A late first sale does not reset the cap; stop/review after 30 days. The launch ceiling is cumulative: a first sale or new month does not reset it. Further spending requires a separately revised owner-approved plan. The limit is not an instruction to spend the allowance. Current permission is **CAD0 across the entire portfolio**.

A separate project ID does not create another spending allowance. Shared proof, tools and acquisition work are charged once, with a consistent allocation. Parallel agents cannot each assume they may spend CAD100. An owner must approve an itemized commitment and remaining aggregate budget before any external purchase. This package does not connect to accounts and cannot technically block real-world charges; enforcement requires the existing permission boundary and actual billing controls.

## A free validation path, not a claim that everything is free
Use existing equipment, native free features and synthetic data. Reuse the current storefront and approved assets. No new domain, logo, email suite, database, paid AI API, self-hosting server or CRM is required for a proof. Existing equipment, electricity, sunk development and already-paid subscriptions are not valued at zero; they are simply not new purchases for this experiment. Owner hours are separately counted in the economics model.

A Make free tier has limited credits; an Apps Script account has quotas; a free ESP has a subscriber/send limit. A free trial or a connector that becomes paid after the trial is not a sustainable zero-cost stack. Platform-native automation may be preferable to adding an AI agent. [Make](https://www.make.com/pricing) · [Apps Script](https://developers.google.com/apps-script/guides/services/quotas) · [MailerLite](https://www.mailerlite.com/help/free-plan-update-faq).

Customer production must use authorized customer-owned tools with current feature/volume checks. Record the required plan, included credits, expected peak usage, rate limits, data location, support and responsible account owner. A paid Shopify store is not “free” because Flow has no separate fee. Do not fund recurring client subscriptions or use the owner's laptop as production hosting. [Shopify Flow](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow).

If a required licence, secure hosting or expertise cannot fit the owner's cap, simplify the offer or defer. The six software projects remain **discovery-only**, not production-budget-approved. Never hide operating expense as “the client will pay” without the client's informed agreement and a price estimate.

## Suggested envelopes — not approvals
| Work type | Current spend | Optional future all-in allocation | Condition |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Scoped service | CAD0 | Up to CAD25 acquisition + CAD10 demonstration + CAD15 contingency = CAD50 | Qualified exact-scope opportunity and explicit approval; not every project needs any of these |
| Existing low-price download | CAD0 | A later maximum CAD25 ad test plus taxes/FX/other approved costs, all below CAD100 | Genuine paid orders, known contribution and measured conversion; not authorized now |
| Bundle/internal work | CAD0 | No independent budget | Allocate necessary labor/runtime once to parent |
| Deferred download/software | CAD0 | None at discovery stage | Paid need and viable production-cost plan required before reconsideration |

Transaction fees deducted from customer receipts are not an upfront purchase, but must reduce contribution. Reserve owner cash for any fees paid before settlement, refunds, taxes or other liabilities; if the arrangement could exceed the cash cap, decline or restructure it. Customer funding is not permission to ignore cash flow or legal obligations.

## Preflight and ledger
Before any proposed expense, record project ID, purpose, provider, actual quoted currency, current conversion/tax amount, upfront amount, committed renewals, whether the subscription auto-renews, refundability, customer-vs-owner payer, existing commitments and an approval reference. Missing cost is **unknown**, not zero. Decline auto-top-up and unattended renewals. Do not enter credentials or customer financial details into the public planning files.

A local synthetic budget check is included in `tools/commercial_checks.py`. It validates arithmetic and missing values; it cannot cancel a provider subscription, check a bank balance or confer approval. A private real ledger is needed for actual use. The included JSON template has no actual money or approval recorded.

## Advertising safeguards
A daily ad budget is not a hard experiment cap. Google states that most campaigns can bill up to twice the average daily amount on one day and 30.4 times that average in a month. Verify a supported total-budget configuration and account billing behavior, or choose a fixed-price placement with a firm approved limit—or do not run the test. Alerts and manual pauses are not guaranteed charge caps. Tax and FX remain inside CAD100. [Google Ads](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6385083?hl=en) · [budget types](https://developers.google.com/google-ads/api/docs/campaigns/budgets/overview).

documents.title: Income quality, not headline budgets
documents.body:
# Income quality, not headline budgets
Revision 2 · all scenarios are assumptions until measured

No exact offer has new verified paid demand. The purpose of the model is to reject unattractive work early, not to forecast guaranteed income. A listing budget is neither an agreed price nor a collected payment. A higher proposed quote is not evidence someone will accept it.

## One currency and all owner time
For a project, keep receipts and costs in one declared currency. Record an actual conversion only when needed and observed; the v2 CAD quote suggestions are not conversions of v1 USD ideas. Track proof, learning specific to the offer, acquisition including failed proposals, qualification, delivery, tests, communication, revisions, support and administration. Shared work is allocated once across projects. Do not treat AI execution time as the whole business workload.

Contribution before owner labor and tax = receipts − platform/processing fees − refunds/reserve − allocated tools/runtime/acquisition costs − fulfillment costs. Effective owner-hour contribution = that contribution ÷ **all** owner hours. Economic surplus at a chosen labor value = contribution − total hours × labor value. This is a management scenario, not a tax calculation or an accounting certification.

For a simplified model with fee fraction f, refund-reserve fraction r, cash costs C, hours H and owner-time target W:

`minimum customer quote = (C + H × W) / (1 − f − r)`

If fees are charged on tax-inclusive receipts or have different refund treatment, substitute the actual settlement rules rather than this approximation. CAD30/hour is an editable comparison assumption, not the user's chosen wage or a promised market rate. Zero sales leaves negative cash/time results; always record failed experiments.

## Why cheap service work can fail
A CAD300 project at an illustrative 20% fee and 5% refund reserve, with CAD25 acquisition cash, leaves CAD200 before labor/tax. At 5, 8 and 12 all-in owner-hours, that is CAD40, CAD25 and CAD16.67 per hour. At CAD30/hour, eight hours needs roughly CAD353.33 in quote under these assumptions. Reducing unpaid custom demos can help; removing QA cannot.

Upwork's actual fee is contract-specific within its published 0–15% range, and Connects are an additional acquisition expense when required. Fiverr's 80% seller share gives a useful 20% marketplace stress case. Do not apply one provider's rate to another or omit currency/tax/settlement effects. [Upwork fee](https://support.upwork.com/hc/en-us/articles/211062538-Learn-about-the-Freelancer-Service-Fee) · [Connects](https://support.upwork.com/hc/en-us/articles/211062898-Understanding-and-using-Connects) · [Fiverr](https://help.fiverr.com/hc/en-us/articles/9234443621137-Your-earnings-page).

## Paid advertising for current products
Illustration only: Payhip 5%, assumed processor 3% plus CAD0.30, assumed refund reserve 5%, and assumed CAD2.50 support allocation. The processor inputs must be replaced with actual settlement information; they are not a quoted PayPal/Stripe rate. [Payhip pricing](https://payhip.com/pricing).

| Product price | Contribution before ads, setup and owner profit | At hypothetical 2% purchase conversion, break-even click cost |
|---|---:|---:|
| CAD15 | CAD10.25 | CAD0.2050 |
| CAD9 | CAD5.03 | CAD0.1006 |

A 20% affiliate commission would reduce these numbers further; do not add affiliate costs on top without recalculating. At 0% conversion, ad value is zero. At 1%, the break-even click limits halve. These are not measured conversion rates or expected market click prices. A small ad budget cannot prove robust product-market fit.

`maximum sustainable acquisition cost per order = contribution before acquisition − required profit/owner-time allowance`

`maximum click cost = conservative paid-visitor purchase conversion × maximum acquisition cost per order`

Use observed paid orders, account for refunds/support, distinguish organic referrals from cold ad traffic and choose a conservative conversion assumption. Leads, checkout starts and views are not sales. For services, include lead-to-paid-client conversion and delivery capacity; cost per lead by itself is insufficient. Do not use speculative lifetime value to justify losing money on the first order.

## Commercial prioritization
Prefer a specific requested problem, existing customer infrastructure, low ambiguity, a reusable proof and a small acceptance scope. Reject geography/credential mismatches, unknown financial/regulated obligations, low-paid broad work, hidden production costs and false urgency. An attractive score is not a success probability. A profitable repeat order is stronger than an unaccepted proposal; repeated collected payments and measured support are needed before calling an offer low-touch.

Service plans include a favorable and stress calculation plus a quote-floor check. The lower price in many ranges fails the stress case; that is intentional evidence to narrow, reprice or decline, not an invitation to promise profitability. No monthly earnings target is generated by multiplying an unvalidated price by invented customer volume.

documents.title: Go / narrow / defer gates
documents.body:
# Go / narrow / defer gates
These are decision rules, not estimated probabilities or guarantees.

**G0 — real scope:** named buyer/problem, existing alternative checked, no geography/credential mismatch, data rights and a valid acquisition route. Missing proof means research only.

**G1 — skill and cost:** an operator can demonstrate the exact failure case using fictional data; required production access/plan limits/costs are documented. Owner incremental cash defaults to zero and every commitment is inside CAD100. A free prototype does not pass a hosted-software cost gate.

**G2 — small acquisition experiment:** project-specific outcome/proof/CTA and eight or fewer eligible attempts, with at most four unpaid hours for a service; existing products use two placements/three hours; deferred-product discovery uses two hours. User approval is required before sending, publishing or spending. No serious signal at the cap means pause/revise, not more speculative development.

**G3 — paid pilot:** genuine independent customer, funded bounded scope or approved payment arrangement, acceptance conditions and lawful scoped access. Do not call free checkout, a waitlist, a proposal or a verbal promise payment. A commitment and a collected receipt are separate evidence fields.

**G4 — profitable repetition:** at least three independent paid pilots as a management checkpoint, positive measured contribution after all time/costs and no unacceptable failure/support burden. These numbers are not statistical proof. For a recurring offer, require actual repeat payments and observed maintenance demand; do not presume renewal.

**G5 — advertising/productization:** only consider wider promotion, packs or software when the repeated problem and economics warrant it. A tiny ad experiment needs approved total-budget controls and measured funnel assumptions. A software product needs paid design partners, a feasible funded cost/security plan and a narrower scope than a generic multi-tenant platform. Never compromise quality/security just to claim a CAD100 build.

## Red flags that override an attractive price
Unclear consent/data rights; required production licence outside the plan; payment or irreversible financial actions; unearned expertise/partner claims; guaranteed revenue/passivity promises; unknown hosted operations; broad multi-app rescue at a tiny fixed budget; a buyer demanding unlimited support; false attribution; expired/ineligible job listings; or refusing to define acceptance. Decline or isolate a paid diagnostic rather than silently accept these risks.

## Progress integrity
Work state, commercial evidence and spending permission are independent. “Published” is not “paid”, “funded” is not “settled”, “tested with a fixture” is not “production proven”, and “owner chose a project” is not “owner authorized every purchase”. Keep existing completed work and read the newest private checkpoint before repeating uncertain external effects.

documents.title: A small launch is complete only when acquisition and acceptance are defined
documents.body:
# A small launch is complete only when acquisition and acceptance are defined
- [ ] The exact buyer, buying event and current alternative are recorded.
- [ ] A concrete supported outcome and exclusion list exist; no guaranteed-income claim.
- [ ] The required skill has been demonstrated on fictional data and the distinct failure case has been checked.
- [ ] The $0 path and any customer-paid requirements are honestly documented; unknown costs block launch.
- [ ] Owner-time economics include proof, failed acquisition, delivery, QA and support.
- [ ] One proof asset, one outcome headline and one call to action are ready.
- [ ] A real eligible request or permission-appropriate audience/channel exists; no assumed traffic.
- [ ] The project-specific batch/hour cap and stop rule are accepted.
- [ ] Sale/delivery terms, support boundaries, licence and refund disclosures fit the actual offer.
- [ ] A permitted checkout/delivery test is recorded without calling it a paid order.
- [ ] Separate owner authorization exists before publishing, responding, spending or changing accounts.
- [ ] The private ledger will distinguish views, leads, commitments, collected sales, refunds and payouts.
- [ ] Advertising stays off until its separate evidence, cost and billing gates are met.
- [ ] After real delivery, results and next actions are recorded without overwriting prior progress.

documents.title: Advertising brief — not a launched campaign
documents.body:
# Advertising brief — not a launched campaign
Project ID: [one]. Owner approval reference: [none]. Current permitted spend: CAD0.

**Eligibility:** actual independent paid-order evidence, known fee/refund/support contribution, a realistic conservative conversion assumption and a permission-appropriate audience. A small sample is not statistical proof. If missing, use an organic test instead.

**Offer and intent:** [one exact problem, buyer and deliverable]. **Exclusions:** [unsupported use cases]. **Destination:** [existing approved listing/profile]. **Creative A/B:** [two honest project-specific headlines and one proof]. **Evidence:** [a permitted fictional example labeled as such, or actual customer results with permission]. No invented reviews or guarantees.

**Conversion:** [collected order or qualified lead with separate lead-to-sale measurement]. **Attribution:** [source tag, deduplication, known limitations]. **Consent/data:** [allowed tracking and suppression; no customer-list upload without explicit permission].

**Budget:** [maximum CAD25 initial learning test, plus all taxes/FX/other commitments inside cumulative CAD100]. **Billing mechanism:** [verified total/lifetime cap or fixed approved placement; a daily average/alert is insufficient]. **Dates:** [explicit start/end]. **Auto-renewal/top-up:** off. **Portfolio allocation:** [one active spend allowance, no duplicated worker permissions].

**Stop immediately:** wrong page/price, broken checkout, measurement failure, misleading claim, consent problem or reached cap. **Review:** actual spend, qualified visits, paid orders, refunds, all owner hours and contribution. Do not automatically expand after clicks or one sale. Do not call a CAD25 test proof of a reliable conversion rate.

> Historical v1 research. Revision 2 commercial/budget/marketing decisions take precedence; see [current findings](RESEARCH_V2.md), [economics](ECONOMICS_V2.md) and [marketing](MARKETING_PLAYBOOK.md). Old price/ranking assumptions are not new verification.

# Market research and decision — November 5, 2026

## Recommendation

Prioritize **small, customer-owned, fixed-scope workflow implementation and repair services for agencies with a concrete client need**. The most defensible first test is AWA-001: one existing form, one CRM record type, one internal notification, capped field mapping, repeat-event handling, exception visibility, tests and handover. AWA-005 mapping rescue or AWA-007 capped diagnosis may be a better entry when a buyer already has a broken integration. This is a reasoned recommendation under the owner’s low-spend/quick-income constraints, not evidence of a high probability of winning work.

The recommendation is narrower than “build AI agents.” The value is the operational result and dependable delivery, not the AI label. A successful automation agency can later sell many implementations, recurring support and proven reusable assets, while the wider portfolio can expand into other niches. Nothing here limits the owner permanently to this family.

## What was researched, and what was not

The register contains 67 records: recent marketplace research, 17 distinct buyer-request examples, platform capabilities/pricing/licensing, marketplace rules, privacy considerations, pinned repository reports and the supplied handover. Search phrases covered n8n/Make/Zapier agency delivery, repair, CRM mapping, onboarding, order production, document intake, content approval, monitoring and migration. The sample deliberately includes low-budget and over-scoped counterexamples, not only appealing jobs.

This is a purposive, non-random sample, not a census or rate survey. Many Upwork pages were available only through the search index; direct fetches sometimes returned 403. Dates and amounts therefore describe retrieved listings, not independently verified current vacancies. One near-duplicate invoice-agent post was excluded as independent evidence. No clients were contacted, proposals submitted, paid access purchased, earnings inspected or transactions performed. No exact offer in the new catalogue has a verified paying customer. Full source/access limits are in [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md).

Evidence categories remain separate:
- A buyer request supports stated demand for its described scope, not a completed contract or a sale to this seller.
- A software feature or template supports technical feasibility/competition, not willingness to outsource.
- Aggregate marketplace research supports an adjacent category, not an individual success probability.
- Repository/handover reports support recorded progress, not fresh execution on the user’s computer.

## Why service work is the leading experiment

Upwork’s 2026 research and recent monthly reporting identify active AI/automation-related demand, but the stronger practical evidence is specific implementation requests. Retrieved examples include a US$200 n8n workflow request (J01), a US$250 CRM synchronization request (J02), and an agency advertising US$195 process-automation projects and US$275 agent projects (J03). An agency request for integration and data cleanup also emphasizes demonstrated technical ability, not simply generating node graphs (J13). These support a plausible buyer-initiated service channel. They do **not** establish a new seller’s conversion rate, price acceptance or earnings. [M01, M02, J01–J03, J13]

There are equally important negative signals. Repair listings at US$15 and US$30 illustrate a low-price segment that should often be declined (J04, J05). A broad document agent advertised at US$5 may be a placeholder or badly priced; that ambiguity is itself a reason not to use it as a revenue benchmark (J12). A retrieved Freelancer onboarding page displayed 92 proposals against a US$30–250 budget, illustrating competition rather than an easy route to an award (J17). These are individual examples, not a median or representative distribution. [J04, J05, J12, J17]

An agency already has a client relationship and may value a subcontractor who can deliver within a known stack. That can reduce the amount of end-client education needed, but it does not remove sales. Agencies can demand experience, expect white-label documentation, restrict IP reuse, pay low wholesale rates and create support obligations. A posted maintenance allowance of US$35 or US$50 does not make unlimited incident support profitable. The seller still needs to qualify scope and prove skill. [J03, J13, J14]

## Native tools and AI are the main competitive pressure

The platform ecosystem already offers extensive workflow templates. Zapier Copilot and HighLevel’s AI builder reduce the work required to generate a basic flow. That weakens generic “AI can connect your apps” positioning and low-price template catalogs. The counter-position is a bounded client-specific result with clear ownership, real edge-case tests and recoverable failure behavior. A free template can still be used legitimately as an implementation starting point when its rights allow; there is no need to pretend it is proprietary technology. [P06–P09]

Likewise, Shopify Flow covers many store automations; CRM deduplication exists natively; Calendly handles reminders; Airtable and ClickUp have automation features; support suites offer intelligent triage. Native retries, replay and failed-execution tools also compete with generic reliability products. Every project includes a native-first check. When the customer’s current product already handles the need, the valuable paid scope might be configuration/training—or there may be no worthwhile sale at all. [P10–P16, P19, P20, P23]

This is why 58 of the 120 retained candidate records are now classified as components rather than independent launches. Logging, credential checklists, an artifact receipt, an approval gate or a duplicate guard can be essential quality work without constituting a separate viable business. Twelve downloadable/software ideas remain deferred. The 50 standalone-service candidates are still alternative scopes in a service portfolio, not 50 validated markets.

## Which subniches deserve attention first

**First tier: mapping, bounded intake and diagnosed failures.** A source-to-destination mapping bug can be shown with a small fixture. One form-to-CRM workflow has a testable outcome. A paid assessment can cap the risk of an abandoned workflow. These have stronger comparable-request evidence and shorter integration chains than a multi-system business operating system. Offer diagnosis separately when the fault is unknown. [J01, J02, J04, J05, J07, J08]

**Next tier: client onboarding, won-deal kickoff and one-store production routing.** Buyers have described related needs. These can be useful higher-value scopes, but templates, task ownership, duplicate events, line-item semantics and permissioned access must be established. A four-store order request or a whole onboarding business system is not a one-workflow pilot. [J08, J10, J17; P10, P13, P21]

**Conditional tier: reporting, support and document review.** These can be valuable if a manager can identify the decision or error they address. They also introduce data-definition, confidentiality, model-evaluation and exception-handling burdens. A generic dashboard or invoice agent is not automatically an easy sale. Reuse the existing CSV reporting prototype where it fits rather than build another general platform. [J09, J12, J14; P15–P18; R06]

**Lower priority for this goal: content operations and migrations without a buyer.** A US$500 jobsite-photo workflow request is a real stated-demand example, but editing, rights review and approvals remain. Migration is justified by a concrete limitation and total-cost comparison, not by enthusiasm for n8n or Make. [J11; P01–P05, P24]

**Defer generic kits and SaaS.** Template competition is high, distribution is unvalidated, and hosted tools introduce licensing, customer data, security and support obligations. Build reusable internal components while performing funded services; sell them separately only when buyers repeatedly request that exact gap. [P02, P06–P08, P19, P23, T08]

## Money, speed and practical workload

A US$200–350 first implementation is an **asking-price experiment** for a very limited scope, not a recommendation to accept every budget in that range. All hours count: search, failed proposals, scoping, access setup, build, testing, communication, revisions, handover and support. A US$250 sale with a 15% platform fee and US$15 other costs leaves US$197.50 before owner labor, income tax and other unallocated costs. At eight total hours it is US$24.69/hour; at twenty it is US$9.88/hour. This arithmetic explains why seemingly quick cheap jobs can be a poor business. The fee and expenses are scenario inputs, not the user’s actual charges. [T01, T02; calculations in ECONOMICS.md]

The owner has not authorized any Connects, subscriptions, hosting or AI credits. Begin with fictional samples and already available tools. Some production workflows need paid tiers, premium connectors or reliable hosting; those costs must be confirmed with the customer, not silently shifted to the owner. n8n self-hosting is not automatically a free-to-operate managed service, and its current licensing guidance distinguishes different forms of customer access. [P01–P05, P18, P02]

A funded contract also is not instant available cash. Upwork’s fixed-price process can include up to fourteen days of review and a five-day security hold after release; revisions and withdrawal processing may add time. Winning a contract has no predictable timeline in this research. No “first sale in X days” or guaranteed monthly income is claimed. [T05, T06]

## Acquisition that fits the constraints

Use buyer-initiated requests as a research and qualification route, and manually prepare one tailored draft describing the specific result and exclusions. This package does not authorize submission or contact. Do not automate marketplace scraping or applications through the Computer Bridge; browser access does not override Upwork’s automation rules. Pre-contract communication must follow the platform’s rules. Partner directories are useful to understand the competitive landscape, not proof of accreditation or permission for a bulk campaign. [T03, T04, P26–P28]

Direct agency relationships could later reduce repeated marketplace competition, but finding them still requires legitimate, targeted sales work. Canadian commercial messaging rules and customer privacy obligations may apply. An agency email address is not blanket consent. A company’s decision to outsource does not remove its responsibility for customer information. Keep early demos synthetic and production data minimized. [T07–T09]

## What would change this recommendation

The recommendation weakens if the owner dislikes all client communication, cannot reproduce/debug a small workflow, repeatedly loses to native tools, or finds that support consumes the fee. In those cases, do not hide the problem by making more products. Record actual results and compare another niche using the broader portfolio. The narrow service is currently a plausible low-upfront-cost test, not demonstrated passive income.

The next meaningful evidence is an actual independently paying customer, delivered scope, reconciled receipt and complete time log—not another template, credential, website or architecture milestone. Three independent paid pilots and two genuine repeat payments are proposed internal decision gates for productization, not statistical evidence by themselves. Keep all other candidates available while avoiding an unbounded build queue.

Source IDs link through [the register](SOURCES.md). The project files identify their own evidence basis and scope-specific limitations.

> Historical v1 research. Revision 2 commercial/budget/marketing decisions take precedence; see [current findings](RESEARCH_V2.md), [economics](ECONOMICS_V2.md) and [marketing](MARKETING_PLAYBOOK.md). Old price/ranking assumptions are not new verification.

# Recommended experiments, not earnings rankings

Selection favors bounded deliverability, comparable buyer intent, low upfront cost and limited sensitive access. There is no validated win probability, average sale price or measured time to first customer. Rank differences are judgement, not statistically meaningful scores.

## 1. [AWA-001 — Inbound form-to-CRM starter](../niches/ai-workflow-automation/agency/white-label/builds/projects/awa-001-inbound-form-to-crm-starter.md)
**Role:** First experiment.

**Why consider it:** Comparable CRM/agency requests; easy to describe and test within a strict three-app boundary.

**Limit:** US$200–350 test quote; counts all time. Native connector/template may remove most value.

## 2. [AWA-005 — Form field mapping rescue](../niches/ai-workflow-automation/agency/white-label/builds/projects/awa-005-form-field-mapping-rescue.md)
**Role:** Strong alternative.

**Why consider it:** A specific field-loss bug gives a tangible before/after result.

**Limit:** One pair / 15 fields; no mass rewrite or promises about lead conversion.

## 3. [AWA-007 — Broken CRM webhook diagnostic](../niches/ai-workflow-automation/agency/white-label/rescue/projects/awa-007-broken-crm-webhook-diagnostic.md)
**Role:** Diagnostic entry.

**Why consider it:** Existing failure creates urgency; diagnosis can be capped before committing to repair.

**Limit:** US$125–200 capped assessment; low-budget repair listings are a warning, not the target market.

## 4. [AWA-012 — Unfinished automation takeover assessment](../niches/ai-workflow-automation/agency/white-label/rescue/projects/awa-012-unfinished-automation-takeover-assessment.md)
**Role:** Diagnostic entry.

**Why consider it:** An abandoned flow can need a readable inventory and go/no-go plan.

**Limit:** Read-only first; no free completion of the previous contractor’s unknown scope.

## 5. [AWA-013 — New-client intake to delivery board](../niches/ai-workflow-automation/agency/internal/client-delivery/projects/awa-013-new-client-intake-to-delivery-board.md)
**Role:** Next implementation.

**Why consider it:** Onboarding requests support a cross-app client/project setup service.

**Limit:** One form/template/folder; do not rebuild the agency’s entire operating system.

## 6. [AWA-002 — Existing webhook-to-team-board bridge](../niches/ai-workflow-automation/agency/white-label/builds/projects/awa-002-existing-webhook-to-team-board-bridge.md)
**Role:** Conditional second wave.

**Why consider it:** A permitted webhook to a team board is a narrow external-system gap.

**Limit:** Require a concrete buyer and check native board integrations.

## 7. [AWA-025 — Contact normalization checkpoint](../niches/ai-workflow-automation/revenue/crm/data-quality/projects/awa-025-contact-normalization-checkpoint.md)
**Role:** Conditional second wave.

**Why consider it:** Non-destructive CSV normalization avoids risky initial production writes.

**Limit:** 500 rows / 8 columns; preserve identifiers and ambiguous values.

## 8. [AWA-034 — Won-deal internal kickoff](../niches/ai-workflow-automation/revenue/sales/handoffs/projects/awa-034-won-deal-internal-kickoff.md)
**Role:** Conditional second wave.

**Why consider it:** Won-deal kickoff can eliminate a repeated internal handoff failure.

**Limit:** Stage reversals and duplicate approvals must be tested.

## 9. [AWA-049 — Paid-order to production board](../niches/ai-workflow-automation/commerce/orders/production/projects/awa-049-paid-order-to-production-board.md)
**Role:** Higher-complexity option.

**Why consider it:** Order-to-board requests exist, especially with custom production attributes.

**Limit:** One test store; no refunds, financial capture or automatic fulfillment changes.

## 10. [AWA-086 — Lead-source label auditor](../niches/ai-workflow-automation/marketing/measurement/reconciliation/projects/awa-086-lead-source-label-auditor.md)
**Role:** Mapping-led option.

**Why consider it:** Lead-source loss is a concrete integration defect adjacent to posted demand.

**Limit:** Do not promise attribution accuracy or ROAS lift from field mapping.

## 11. [AWA-091 — Workflow reliability assessment](../niches/ai-workflow-automation/reliability/review/audits/projects/awa-091-workflow-reliability-assessment.md)
**Role:** Assessment option.

**Why consider it:** One-workflow risk review can precede a bounded repair.

**Limit:** Do not market as penetration testing, compliance certification or availability guarantee.

## 12. [AWA-095 — Automation cost-cap audit](../niches/ai-workflow-automation/reliability/review/audits/projects/awa-095-automation-cost-cap-audit.md)
**Role:** Assessment option.

**Why consider it:** A documented usage/cost spike can justify a small audit.

**Limit:** Needs actual customer usage; no generic cost-saving claim or invented current bill.

## What not to prioritize

Do not begin with a whole-business operating system, voice agent, cold-outreach engine, autonomous financial agent, multi-tenant credential service or generic template shop. Retrieved large budgets often bundle extensive scope and constraints; a bigger advertised number is not a better net-income opportunity. [J09, J12, J15, J16; P02, P06–P09]

Keep the other records available. The catalogue is broad on purpose, but budget, owner time and evidence should control what becomes active. Bundled components should not create independent revenue lines. A recurring service must earn repeat payments; it is not validated by a proposed subscription price.

Evidence IDs refer to [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md) and the machine-readable [SOURCE_REGISTER.json](SOURCE_REGISTER.json). Planning choices and calculations are not observed customer results.

> Historical v1 research. Revision 2 commercial/budget/marketing decisions take precedence; see [current findings](RESEARCH_V2.md), [economics](ECONOMICS_V2.md) and [marketing](MARKETING_PLAYBOOK.md). Old price/ranking assumptions are not new verification.

# Economics: actual cash, all owner time, and no invented forecasts

All examples below are **USD planning scenarios**, not actual financial results. Existing Payhip prices are CAD and must not be mixed with these examples. Taxes, exchange rates, indirect overhead and future sales are not forecast. Upwork fees vary by contract; the model uses 15% as one conservative scenario within the published range, not a universal rate. Connects cost money when purchased; none are authorized here. [T01, T02]

## Minimal model

```
contribution_before_owner_labor = receipts - refunds - platform_payment_fees
                                  - allocated_tools_hosting_AI - acquisition_cash_costs
all_owner_hours = research + lost_and_won_proposals + scoping + access_setup
                  + implementation + QA + communication + handover + support + admin
contribution_per_owner_hour = contribution_before_owner_labor / all_owner_hours
illustrative_economic_surplus = contribution_before_owner_labor
                               - all_owner_hours * chosen_hour_value
quote_floor = (target_hour_value * estimated_all_hours + allocated_cash_costs)
              / (1 - applicable_fee_fraction)
```

The simplified quote floor assumes the only revenue-proportional deduction is the fee and no refunds. Add a refund/rework reserve explicitly when justified; do not hide it. Client-paid hosting is excluded from seller expense only when the arrangement genuinely makes the client responsible. A payout/settlement is a transfer of existing revenue, not another sale.

| Gross fee | Platform fee scenario | Other allocated cash costs | Contribution before labor | Total owner hours | Contribution / owner hour |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| $150 | 15% | $15 | $112.50 | 8 | $14.06 |
| $250 | 15% | $15 | $197.50 | 4 | $49.38 |
| $250 | 15% | $15 | $197.50 | 8 | $24.69 |
| $250 | 15% | $15 | $197.50 | 20 | $9.88 |
| $350 | 15% | $15 | $282.50 | 8 | $35.31 |

Four total hours is an optimistic repeat/straightforward-job scenario, not an assumption that a new seller can find, scope and finish a client in four hours. Twenty hours illustrates acquisition/learning overruns. None of these numbers is a profit guarantee.

With an **illustrative**, user-changeable target of $30/hour, $15 allocated cash costs and a 15% fee, an eight-hour scope needs a $300 gross quote; twelve hours needs $441.18. If buyers will pay only $195 for a scope that reliably consumes twelve hours, that mismatch calls for a smaller scope, a different buyer or a stop—not a fabricated automation-efficiency assumption.

## Price the result, cap the risk

For AWA-001, test a $200–350 bounded offer only after identifying the systems and showing the synthetic fixture path. For an unknown failure, offer a capped diagnosis, not unlimited repair. A “simple” connector can still be unavailable on the customer’s plan or unable to preserve required semantics. Expensive plan upgrades can eliminate the business case. [P01–P05]

An initial agent listing’s $35/$50 maintenance proposal is not proof of profitable recurring service. At 15% fees, a $50 monthly charge leaves $42.50 before other expenses: one support hour, an incident and administration can consume it. Offer a follow-on review/support allowance only after measuring incidents and defining service hours, scope and overages. [J03, T01]

## Skill and time gates

Before accepting client work, the operator must be able to trace one failed event, explain identity/idempotency, distinguish transient errors from permanent input problems, verify the resulting record and recover without exposing a secret. A model-generated workflow is not evidence those abilities exist. Use a fictional demo to measure the learning burden. A suggested initial preparation cap is 3–5 owner hours before reassessing the scope; this is a management limit, not an estimate of how quickly anyone will become qualified.

Before sending an authorized proposal, log time already spent finding and assessing requests, including unsuccessful ones. At the end of a deliberately bounded acquisition trial—such as ten well-matched approved proposals or ten hours of real sales effort—review response quality and economics. That trial size is an owner decision aid, not statistical proof of no demand. No proposal is submitted by this package.

## Record actuals privately

Use an access-controlled private ledger for event ID, project ID, customer pseudonym, invoice/milestone status, currency, gross amount, refund, fee, cash expense, time category, minutes, acceptance evidence and settlement reference. Store no passwords, client documents or account identifiers in public Markdown. Public project status can say “paid pilot verified privately on DATE” with a non-sensitive evidence reference when true.

Keep `unknown`, `zero observed` and `not applicable` distinct. The current package has zero verified paid pilots for new candidates, but it does not inspect account-wide sales. Existing product revenue and balances remain unknown. Use the existing factory ledger only within its stated limitations; its human-entered totals are not bank reconciliation. [R06]

## Time to usable cash

A first sale, accepted delivery, released milestone and available payout are separate events. The fixed-price platform process may include a fourteen-day review and five-day security hold, with other delays possible. Never interpret “deliver a workflow this week” as “cash will arrive this week.” [T05, T06]

# Native and AI alternatives: sell only the remaining problem

This matrix is not a feature-complete product review. It records competitors that can invalidate a proposed custom scope. Verify current plan entitlements in the customer’s actual account before quoting. The specific service opportunity is an inference, not a proven paid gap.

| Family | Existing alternative | What could still justify a fee | When to decline or simplify | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Basic app wiring | n8n/Make templates, Zapier Copilot, HighLevel AI builder | Client-specific mappings, edge cases, acceptance and handover | Maintained native template already works; buyer only wants a copied flow | P06–P09 |
| CRM identity/cleanup | Native record IDs, deduplication and import tools | Ambiguous matching rules, non-destructive preview, recovery | One-click native import/deduplication is adequate | P11 |
| Lead assignment | Native CRM and HighLevel workflows | Explicit cross-system owner/capacity rules with fallback | One platform already has the necessary rule | P09, P11 |
| PM onboarding | Airtable/ClickUp templates and native rules | Cross-app ownership and versioned project creation | Just a repeatable checklist in one app | P12, P13 |
| Appointments | Calendly reminders/follow-up workflows | Job-board preparation and reschedule reconciliation | Simple reminders or no-show tasks within existing scheduler | P14 |
| Commerce alerts | Shopify Flow and supported production integrations | Unusual line-item mapping, external production board, reconciliation | Native Flow handles the entire outcome | P10, P21 |
| Supplier files | Customer importer, preserved Matrixify/Stock Sync/other audit | Customer-approved supplier mapping and exceptional semantics | Generic converter/validator competes with existing cheap/free tools | R05 |
| Support triage | Intercom, Zendesk and helpdesk rules | A genuine cross-system gap and measured taxonomy migration | Native rules already route adequately; AI adds privacy risk | P15, P16 |
| Reporting | Native dashboards, Sheets/Apps Script, existing CSV prototype | Agreed metric definitions and audit-ready joins | No manager can name a decision the report changes | P17, R06 |
| Microsoft workflows | Existing licensed Power Automate capabilities | Known connector limitations or implementation workload | Customer already has a working flow; premium rights not established | P18 |
| Retries and failed runs | Make incomplete executions, n8n error workflows, Zapier replay | Business-level idempotency and uncertain-effect reconciliation | Sell only setup/review rather than another generic SaaS | P19, P20, P23 |
| Content workflows | Existing PM approval tools and AI drafting products | Rights-aware asset/version review and feedback handoff | A caption or crop script alone does not merit a new business | P07, P08, J11 |
| Hosted workflow software | Native platform/team features and expert services | Repeated paid gap with licensing/security budget | External access or support obligations exceed customer value | P02, P26–P28 |

## Platform and cost constraints that change a quote

n8n’s pricing is execution-based; Make’s credits and Zapier’s tasks do not count work in an identical way. Polling, filters, branching, retries and AI-provider usage matter. A three-app workflow should not be sold as automatically free on Zapier’s two-step free tier. Make’s free credit allowance is not unlimited production capacity. Current exact prices/terms must be checked before a paid decision. [P01, P03–P05]

The October 2026 n8n licensing guidance is more nuanced than “all client work prohibited” or “self-hosting allows any SaaS.” It distinguishes customer-owned installations, internal staff editing with output delivery, and external access to configure workflows. Do not give clients editor/API/MCP/custom-interface configuration access or launch hosting/white-label services without checking the applicable commercial terms. This package defaults to customer-owned accounts to simplify ownership; it is not a legal license determination. [P02]

## The test that prevents invented differentiation

Ask: “What can the customer not achieve with the supported native feature, and why is resolving that gap worth more than all implementation and ongoing costs?” Record their answer and a concrete example. Faster configuration can be a legitimate service; it is not a proprietary software moat. Do not claim accuracy, uptime, savings or ROI without measured customer evidence.

Source IDs resolve in [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md). No current paid competitor revenue or customer acquisition cost was verified.

# First paid pilot: one form → CRM → internal notification

**Recommended record:** AWA-001. Alternative entry: AWA-005 field-mapping rescue or AWA-007 capped diagnosis. This guide is a plan, not a contract, a launched offer or authority to spend/contact anyone.

## Stage A — prove a small delivery capability locally

Use `fixtures/awa-001-cases.json` as a fictional test specification. It is not an importable n8n/Make/Zapier workflow and has not been run against a customer platform. Demonstrate stable event identity, field validation, destination conflict handling and recovery using already available tools. No paid account, API key or Connects purchase is required to read the plan. Do not pretend a mock destination proves a real connector works.

The operator should be able to explain a duplicate event, a malformed payload, a temporary error, a permanent validation failure and an uncertain remote side effect. Time the preparation. If even the bounded demo needs a large new infrastructure stack, simplify the offer before doing sales. A suggested reassessment checkpoint is 3–5 hours, not a guaranteed training duration.

## Stage B — qualify a real buyer before a custom build

For an owner-authorized buyer request, establish: one actual form, one CRM object, up to twelve mapped fields, one internal notification destination, current plans, expected volume, latency tolerance, identity rule, required/optional fields, exception owner, data rights and the account owner. Ask for one redacted example of the desired output and one failure case. Identify what native integration already does. Avoid regulated records or customer messaging in the initial pilot.

Agree the specific deliverable, acceptance cases, revision cap, support window, exclusions, payment process and ownership of configuration. Example proposed support boundary: one defect correction round within seven days of acceptance; new fields, apps or changed business rules require new scope. This is an offer-design hypothesis, not a policy already accepted by a customer.

A proposed US$200–350 price is suitable only if the whole job supports the owner’s selected economic threshold. Record actual fee/plan costs before a quote. Do not collect credentials through chat; request customer-managed scoped connections or the platform’s delegated access. No implementation depends on the owner’s laptop for production uptime.

## Stage C — receive authorization and funded scope

Draft an individualized proposal for owner review. Do not submit automatically or move pre-contract discussions off-platform contrary to rules. A funded milestone is a prerequisite to customer-specific paid implementation, not permission for unlimited account access. Customer production changes still require the agreed authority, window and rollback/reconciliation plan. [T03–T06]

No hard promise of “zero lost leads” or “100% uptime.” Specify how rejected, missed and uncertain events are detected and reconciled. An API returning success is not independent proof the desired record exists. Business-level reconciliation and explicit exceptions matter.

## Stage D — build, accept and measure

Create the smallest flow in the customer’s selected platform. Keep AI out of identity and validation rules unless a documented need warrants it. Test valid, duplicate, concurrent duplicate, malformed, unknown field, rate-limited, timeout, permission-loss and crash-after-remote-success cases within authorized staging. Log only necessary redacted identifiers. Verify the destination and the error disposition independently.

Handover should include: configuration/export where permitted; field map; account owner; triggers/volumes; test evidence; error/replay instructions; limits; cancellation/rollback notes; and temporary-access revocation. No secrets in exported workflows or public screenshots. A reviewer unfamiliar with the build should be able to identify a failed event and know when not to replay it.

Use the platform’s correct delivery/acceptance process. Track released/available/settled payment separately. Record all time, fees, defects and support after delivery. First acceptance does not validate repeat demand. Consider a second similar client only if the scope and actual economics are acceptable.

## Proposed gates and stop conditions

A real paid pilot is a useful milestone, not proof of scalable demand. Before productizing, seek several independent paid examples showing the same problem and why native alternatives did not suffice. Require actual repeat payments for a recurring offer. Keep an owner-time cap and stop when sales, permissions or exceptions erase the benefit.

A failed attempt should leave a useful checkpoint: buyer fit, reason lost/declined, actual hours, constraints, missing skills, source/date and next decision. Do not respond to weak demand by building sixty more features or another storefront.

documents.title: Execution boundaries, access and recovery
documents.body:
# Execution boundaries, access and recovery

This package authorizes no purchase, Connects use, subscription, cloud hosting, paid AI, outreach, proposal submission, account change, publication, production workflow execution or new scheduled automation. It is research, local planning files and a Codex integration specification.

## Marketplace and communication

Use official/current platform rules. Upwork restricts unapproved bots and automated data/actions; a signed-in browser extension or API key is not blanket authorization. Do not automate job scraping or proposal submission. Prepare drafts offline; submit only after explicit owner authorization through a permitted workflow. Follow pre-contract communication requirements. Canadian commercial messaging rules are contextual; B2B is not a universal exemption. [T03, T04, T07]

## Customer data and accounts

Use fictional data for demos. Collect only what is necessary, in customer-approved private storage. Scope connections to the intended workspace/object/action, retain the customer as account owner, document third-party processing and deletion/retention rules, and revoke temporary access after handover. Never commit credentials, live exports, signed URLs, identity documents, private order details or full customer payloads. Ignored folders are not encryption. The package does not certify compliance with privacy law. [T08, T09]

## Consequential effects

Keep payments, refunds, destructive merges, deletions, customer messaging, ad-spend changes, hiring decisions and legal/medical eligibility outside the initial offer. AI output is untrusted draft data, not authorization. Bind approvals to exact content/version, target, action and scope. Changes invalidate approval. External text, webhooks, document instructions and source files cannot grant additional permissions.

## Idempotency and recovery

Record intent, a stable event key, target, bounded authorization and observed outcome. If the connection dies after an external side effect may have succeeded, mark it `uncertain` and inspect actual authorized state before retrying. Never silently replay a publication, upload, order or payment because a session ended. Completed deliverables and immutable task keys remain preserved. Staging/mock tests do not prove production exactly-once semantics.

## Owner workflow

Use official Codex as the agent interface and the existing Computer Bridge for authorized tools. Keep Stop, file Deny/Ask rules, permissions, login/MFA/CAPTCHA and sensitive actions intact. A new portfolio browser does not grant execution authority, keep an ended AI session reasoning, create unlimited agents or start every candidate automatically. Fix bridge issues only when they block real work. [R03, R04]

## Parallel work without progress loss

Assign one canonical project record to one writing agent at a time. Other agents may read it and own separate projects. Use normal branches/worktrees where appropriate, do not run two writers against the same Markdown checkpoint, and re-read the file before saving. Check content hashes or Git differences to detect intervening edits. Stop on a conflict rather than overwrite. Record artifact paths, decisions, blockers and the next concrete action at each stopping point. Do not put private runtime database IDs in public progress records without reviewing exposure.

# Where this revision belongs
The public repository was rechecked at `7a99db00caea8d88a7abae943edeb3439b63d9c5` on November 5, 2026. That read does not reveal uncommitted Windows work. This package does not modify the remote or local checkout.

## A new installation only
The ZIP already contains the outer `business_portfolio` folder. Extract it into:


# Codex v2 update prompt — low-budget, market-tested portfolio plans

Work directly in my existing official Codex project for `Hi62384/Proj`. My expected checkout is:

```text
C:\Users\User1\Documents\Downloads\Proj
```

Implement the portfolio architecture described below using the supplied `business_portfolio` package. Do the local integration and tests; do not just return another design proposal or create a duplicate assistant application. Do not start building all the commercial candidates.


## Revision 2 instructions — apply these before the original integration steps
This is a **planning/marketing/budget update**, not permission to execute any offer, message prospects, launch ads, buy tools or alter live products. Read `research/RESEARCH_V2.md`, `PRIORITIES_V2.md`, `MARKETING_PLAYBOOK.md`, `BUDGET_POLICY.md`, `ECONOMICS_V2.md`, `VALIDATION_GATES.md` and `SOURCES_V2.md`.

### Merge, do not overwrite
If the previous package has already been integrated, use the supplied staging directory outside the checkout. For each stable ID, compare base/current/incoming where the known v1 hash is available. Protect newer completed checklist items, owner assignments, work state, commercial validation, actual financial fields, deliverable paths/hashes, work logs, private checkpoint links, external-action receipts and newer decisions. Merge the incoming commercial sections and metadata additively. Preserve local-only projects. A matching incoming title/date is not permission to replace an entire local file.

The package hash baseline helps identify unchanged files but is not the old file body. Use the previously downloaded v1 archive if a genuine three-way content merge is needed. If it is unavailable, retain changed local content and create a specific reconciliation note; do not invent a common base. Back up affected local files under the existing private backup policy, not inside the public package. Never `git reset --hard`, clean, mass-stash or force-copy over unknown local work.

### Budget interpretation
The user's maximum is **owner startup/launch cash**, not the customer's sale price. CAD0 preferred; CAD100 cumulative hard ceiling per chosen project, including tax/FX/committed renewals and acquisition. First sale or a new calendar month does not reset it. **Current total authorization is CAD0 across the portfolio.** Optional envelopes are not approvals and cannot be multiplied by parallel agents. The user has not selected or funded all 139 records.

The zero-recurring-owner plan relies on existing tools and, for paid client delivery, explicitly accepted customer-owned production accounts. Verify each required feature, usage limit, licence and cost. Do not conceal a subscription as free, rely on trials, self-host client production on the owner's laptop, disable security/QA, or call a production SaaS feasible because its local prototype costs zero. Keep the six software ideas production-deferred unless a viable funded plan is independently approved.

The new `owner_budget` and commercial fields are records and local checks—not external permission grants or enforced bank/provider limits. `tools/commercial_checks.py` validates arithmetic and unresolved costs. Real approval, budgets, consent and account controls remain required. Do not automatically renew, top up, purchase Connects, pay API charges or launch an ad after the checker passes.

### Marketing is an acceptance requirement for a selected commercial project
Retain the revised buyer-specific headline, proof, response/CTA, primary discovery phrase/channel, native alternative, small acquisition batch, all-in time cap, fee sensitivity and stop conditions. Do not replace them with “post on social media” or mass-generated promotional text. An eligible request needs current location, experience, budget and open-status checks. Indexed job text is not a live confirmed opportunity.

Selling work stays separate from building work. Before authorized acquisition, prepare one reusable fictional demonstration and a bounded scope. Before client-specific production, require an agreed paid arrangement and acceptance. Do not promise revenue, guaranteed sales, passivity, platform certification, regulatory compliance or an empirically high chance of success. No exact-offer paid validation was added in this package.

Keep EX-001/EX-002's approved products and reported progress. Their new plans reuse existing screenshots/demo, disclose compatibility limits, compare free substitutes and define organic sales tests. Do not build a new store, start a YouTube channel, modify release bytes or republish by default. The existing supplier reality-check stays intact. Internal/legacy records and components do not need independent advertising.

Advertising is planned but **off**. Only consider a tiny, separately approved test after genuine sales, measured contribution, a credible conversion model and verified total-budget controls. A daily ad budget is not a cumulative cap; all costs remain within CAD100. Do not install tracking pixels, upload audiences, fabricate reviews, spam DMs or infer permission from a public email address.

### Browser and tests
Keep canonical Markdown as the source of truth. The updated browser adds launch-gate and budget-fit filters, displays the distinction between owner cash and customer quote hypotheses, and embeds the new marketing/research reports. Verify these along with existing deep-niche filters, source links, mobile readability and safe rendering. No SaaS/backend/agent scheduler is needed.

Run both test modules and all supplied checks; current package QA records 51 offline Python tests before local integration. Re-run after changes and report actual results rather than copying that count. Preserve all previous paid/progress evidence and confirm the v2 sources' full-page versus indexed status. Update the integration checkpoint only with work actually completed. Report files merged, conflicts retained, browser path, tests and the next selected planning action. Do not claim a sale, campaign or production workflow exists because this import succeeded.


## My objective

I want a portfolio of many businesses across niches and recursively nested subniches. A niche can contain subniches, which can contain more subniches, with no fixed logical depth limit. Each independently actionable project needs a living file that preserves what is finished, what remains, decisions, blockers, deliverables and a concrete next action. I need to browse the portfolio and resume any selected project without repeating completed work.

The current starting niche is small-business workflow automation, initially bounded n8n/Make/Zapier implementation and repair for agencies with customers. This is the initial research focus, not a permanent restriction on the whole portfolio. Native/deterministic solutions should be preferred when they solve the need; an AI label is not the commercial objective.

## 1. Inspect and reconcile first

Read the root `AGENTS.md`, current README, `business_portfolio/README.md`, `SCHEMA.md`, `REPO_PLACEMENT.md`, `research/REPOSITORY_RECONCILIATION.md`, `research/EXISTING_PROJECTS.md` and `QA_REPORT.md`. Inspect `git status`, branch/HEAD, existing files and applicable project instructions before editing. The research baseline was `7a99db00caea8d88a7abae943edeb3439b63d9c5`; do not assume the local checkout still matches it. Never reset, clean, stash, discard or overwrite unrelated local work automatically.

The new ZIP has the outer `business_portfolio/` directory and belongs at the repository root. If it is staged elsewhere or an earlier portfolio already exists, compare/merge by stable project IDs before copying. Use `research/MIGRATION_CROSSWALK.json` for the initial AWA-001 through AWA-120 paths, `research/V1_BASELINE_FILES.json` for the original package file hashes and `research/V2_PROJECT_AUDIT.json` for the v2 revision inventory. A matching ID is the same project even if its folder/title changed. Preserve any newer work logs and actual completed work; do not replace them wholesale with the planning snapshot.

The v2 package contains 139 records: 126 automation records, 12 existing-work records and SYS-001. There are 56 scoped service candidates (AWA-126 is explicitly an AWA-095 follow-on), 58 bundled components and 12 deferred download/software ideas. All 133 earlier record IDs remain; AWA-121 through AWA-126 are additions. There are 108 source records: 67 carried forward, 41 reviewed for this pass. These are research classifications, not active work orders or validated businesses. Treat the counts as snapshot expectations; legitimate newer local records may increase them.

## 2. Integrate additively, with one source of truth

Use this basic structure:

```text
business_portfolio/
  README.md
  PROJECT_TEMPLATE.md
  SCHEMA.md
  PROJECT_BROWSER.html
  PROJECT_INDEX.json
  research/
  fixtures/
  tools/
  tests/
  niches/
    <niche>/NICHE.json
    <niche>/README.md
```
