```text
    <niche>/<subniche>/...
```

Reuse and inspect the provided standard-library builder/browser rather than replacing them with a web framework, database, cloud backend, package-manager stack or another AI app. Keep the browser usable through `file://` without a server or API key. A niche may hold projects and child niches simultaneously. There must be no hardcoded “category/subcategory” depth ceiling. Respect Windows path/reserved-name limits with short slugs.

Canonical project records are Markdown with strict JSON frontmatter between `---` delimiters. Generated index/HTML must never become a second editable progress database. Read `SCHEMA.md` and preserve stable project and niche IDs. A niche rename/move changes its path and immediate-parent reference as needed, not its identity. Validate unknown/duplicate IDs, invalid paths, missing parents, cycles, malformed metadata, invalid state values and unresolved source/project references. Keep symlinks/private directories outside indexing.

Add a small root README navigation link to the new portfolio while retaining the Opportunity Library and current product links. Add a narrowly scoped section to existing project instructions explaining where canonical project records live and how agents checkpoint them; preserve all unrelated instructions. Add an existing dashboard link only if it is a small, compatible change—do not make desktop integration a large prerequisite to using the offline browser.

## 3. Preserve research and existing projects

Do not move/delete/rewrite the original `opportunity_library/`, `buissiness_research/`, `research_merge/`, product folders, launch outputs, master execution manual, source archives, private releases or legacy tools merely to make the new folders look tidy. `buissiness_research` is the actual spelling. Link to existing sources; promote a legacy candidate only after explicit selection and identity review. Do not create 1,512 active project tasks from the research library.

Reconcile these existing records against newer authorized local evidence:

- EX-001 cleaning calculator: reported public at CA$15; current v1.0.1 customer release and buyer hash recorded; Calc/file-format checks are not native Excel certification; paid demand/charged payment/payout unverified. Preserve current delivered bytes, not an unreviewed rebuild of authoring sources.
- EX-002 inventory planner: reported public at CA$9; final v1.0.1 filename; free-order delivery and buyer matching reported; native Excel and paid behavior unverified. Output is a reorder threshold/gap, not optimized order quantity. Recover actual private release path/hash locally if needed; do not invent them.
- EX-003 legal-name Payhip storefront/support: reuse existing store, PayPal connection, policies and contact setup. Old Cedargrid links and hidden CA$29/CA$19 test states are historical. Do not republish, rebrand or redo checkout tests just because a new chat started.
- EX-004 cleaning demo: reported 70-second captioned video, unpublished/private. Reuse only as an EX-001 proof asset after its actual private file is located and checked. Do not restart the withdrawn YouTube-channel proposal or recreate a missing video by default.
- EX-005 supplier service: preserve the reality check. K05/B01/K01/J01 are components of one unvalidated experiment, not four markets. Do not build its 96-entry catalog. Link overlapping AWA catalog modules rather than double-counting them.
- EX-006 synthetic reporting prototype: preserve its real existing builder and schema limitations; no paid customers are established. Recover an actual legacy ID only from evidence, never guess.
- EX-007 Computer Bridge: current internal tool, not a new commercial launch. Official Codex remains the interface.
- EX-008/009 Relay and standalone assistant: retained legacy. Preserve historical state/shared modules, do not revive these as the normal work interface.
- EX-010 Opportunity Library: preserve 1,512 research records and IDs; none automatically becomes commercially validated.
- EX-011 factory: preserve .local state, draft-only boundaries and unreconciled manual ledger semantics.
- EX-012 VaultDesk: inventory-only, progress unknown and unrelated. Do not restart or modify it without a separate task.
- SYS-001: update the integration checkpoint with changes/tests actually performed. Mark local integration complete only when its stated acceptance criteria pass.

Do not invent percent-complete numbers, actual revenue, orders, test results or progress for inaccessible private files. A checkmark imported from a report remains “reported” until you actually verify it. Keep chronology/conflicts visible; newer evidence may supersede old status without erasing the old record.

## 4. Progress, resuming and parallel work

Keep implementation/work state separate from commercial validation. “Published” does not mean paid demand; “tests passed” does not mean a successful business. Any paid/repeat-validation state requires a meaningful non-sensitive evidence reference to reconciled private records; a field populated by an agent is not proof of payment.

For each selected task, read the project record, relevant sources and latest private checkpoint before acting. Record current objective, completed work, remaining checklist, blockers, important decisions, exact artifact paths/version/hash when useful, test evidence and next action. On pause/interruption, leave a usable checkpoint. Do not regenerate an existing product or replay an upload/publication/order/payment because an earlier session ended.

Use one writer per canonical project record. Re-read and compare expected content/hash before a save, or use appropriate separate worktrees and reconcile changes. Fail visibly on concurrent modification rather than silently overwriting. Independent projects may proceed in parallel only within existing resources and actual authorization. Do not invent unlimited agents or hidden ongoing reasoning.

If a bridge project mapping is genuinely needed, store the mapping privately, preserve existing runtime ownership and IDs, and reuse the bridge’s durable queue/recovery model. Do not auto-create queue jobs for candidate records, re-key completed immutable jobs, wipe SQLite state, widen permissions, disable Stop or grant new browser/file authority. A JSON `execution_authorized` flag is descriptive, not a permission grant.

Uncertain external effects require actual-state reconciliation before retry. Record intent, target, stable event key, authorized scope and observed outcome; preserve ambiguity when it cannot be resolved. No automatic replay of consequential actions after a crash.

## 5. Keep commercial research honest and practical

The source register distinguishes full-page evidence, indexed snippets, repository reports and the handover. Job budgets are not earnings; market interest is not paid validation; template availability proves competition, not demand. Recheck dated or inaccessible evidence before consequential use, without turning this integration into weeks of new research.

The first proposed tests are AWA-005 or AWA-001 (one form → CRM → internal notification), with AWA-005/007/012 as alternative mapping/diagnostic entries. Preparation fixtures are fictional and have `not_run` results; do not label them as an implemented n8n workflow or a passed production test. Existing tools and native platform features should be checked before creating custom code.

The user’s goal is meaningful income with little upfront spending and limited ongoing manual work. Count all acquisition, communication, permissions, QA, rework and support hours. Keep hypothetical prices/hours separate from actual receipts and costs. Do not start a new storefront, SaaS, audience-building campaign or infrastructure overhaul by default.

## 6. Privacy and action boundaries

This task authorizes local architecture/content integration and relevant tests—not buying Connects/subscriptions/API credits/hosting, sending proposals or prospect messages, publishing products, changing accounts, placing orders, moving money or executing customer production workflows. No new recurring/scheduled tasks are implied. Preserve existing platform rules and sensitive-action approvals.

Do not automate Upwork scraping/applications through the bridge. Do not export credentials, signed URLs, real customer payloads, private payment records or paid product packages into this public repository or generated browser. Keep operational data in appropriately protected private storage; `.gitignore` is not encryption. Preserve legal-name storefront choices and existing policies; do not claim legal/tax/privacy/security certification.

Do not modify root-wide settings or unrelated user projects to make the import pass. Do not commit/push or publish changes externally unless my standing permissions for this project actually authorize that action; otherwise leave a tested local diff and report it.

## 7. Test and deliver the integration

Run the supplied checks and fix real failures:

```powershell
python business_portfolio/tools/build_browser.py
python business_portfolio/tools/build_browser.py --check
python -m unittest discover -s business_portfolio/tests -v
python business_portfolio/tools/commercial_checks.py --portfolio business_portfolio
```

Also run only relevant existing suites if their code is touched. Verify the browser in the user’s actual browser: offline open, search by ID/text, filtering a parent niche includes deeper descendants, existing-work filter, readable progress and source references, report view, empty results and mobile-width layout. Check that copied resume prompts identify the correct canonical record and do not grant external authority.

Exercise a temporary deeply nested niche/project fixture; duplicate IDs, invalid metadata/parents, cycles, unsafe URL/script text and unknown source IDs should fail safely or render as inert text. Verify private folders and symlinks are not exposed. Ensure a published-but-unvalidated product displays both states without converting it to “commercially complete.”

Check missing internal links, stale generated views, migration ID coverage and Windows path lengths. Confirm the original product/research paths and current launch links remain intact. Update/reconcile snapshot hashes only for the files you actually changed; never claim the original manifest matches edited content.

When finished, report what was merged, original files preserved, any unresolved local differences, exact browser path, commands/tests actually executed and their results, and the next actionable project recommendation. Distinguish package tests from Windows/bridge/customer/live-account tests. Do not end with an invented claim that the business is launched or money has been earned.

documents.title: Project format and recursive architecture
documents.body:
# Project format and recursive architecture

## Layout

```
business_portfolio/
  README.md
  PROJECT_TEMPLATE.md
  PROJECT_BROWSER.html           generated, read-only, offline
  PROJECT_INDEX.json             generated; never the progress source of truth
  SCHEMA.md
  CODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_PROMPT.md
  REPO_PLACEMENT.md
  QA_REPORT.md
  research/                     evidence, assumptions, reconciliation, crosswalk
  fixtures/                     fictional acceptance specifications, not workflows
  tools/                        standard-library builder + browser template
  tests/                        package tests, not customer workflow tests
  niches/
    <niche>/NICHE.json
    <niche>/README.md
    <niche>/projects/<stable-id>-<title>.md
    <niche>/<child>/NICHE.json
    <niche>/<child>/projects/<stable-id>-<title>.md
    <niche>/<child>/<grandchild>/...
  .local/                       optional private operational references; ignored
```

Any niche can contain projects, child niches, both or neither. There is **no fixed number of nesting levels**. The filesystem is the canonical hierarchy; `NICHE.json` records its identity and parent. OS path/filename limits still apply. Use short lowercase folder slugs and never use `projects`, `private` or `local` as a niche name. Dot-directories and private folders are excluded from browser indexing. Symlinks are rejected rather than followed.

## Niche metadata

`NICHE.json` has `id`, `title`, `parent`, and `path`. IDs such as `N-8c35…` are assigned once and remain immutable on a rename/move. The initial package derives IDs deterministically, but a future rename does not recompute them. `path` is relative to `niches/`; `parent` is the immediate parent niche ID or null at the top level. Parent references, IDs and directory paths must agree. Do not create duplicate directory aliases to make a project appear in several categories; use project links/tags.

## Markdown with JSON frontmatter

Every project begins with `---`, a JSON object, and another `---`. JSON is deliberately used as a strict subset of YAML so Python’s standard library can parse it without PyYAML or permissive object deserialization. No comments, trailing commas, duplicate keys, NaN or Infinity in metadata. Markdown below contains the living human-readable record.

Required fields:
- `id`, `title`, `schema_version` (1), `niche_id`, `niche_path`.
- `record_type`, `origin`, `priority`, `work_state`, `commercial_validation`, `evidence_basis`.
- `source_ids`, `parent_project` (ID or null), `related_projects` (IDs), `next_action`, `last_reviewed` (date).
- `execution_authorized` (boolean), `privacy`.

The supplied records also include historical IDs, owner, hypothetical quote/hour ranges, verified-pilot count and unknown actual revenue/profit. Null means unknown/not established, never zero. `verified_paid_pilots: 0` for candidates means this research verified none; it does not claim to inspect all user accounts.

`record_type` describes whether a record is a standalone service candidate, bundled component, deferred download/software, existing product/tool/operation, inventory-only record or system task. Classification is a planning judgement, not a license or a measured success probability. The browser supports further non-empty record types; add meaningful types rather than duplicating offers.

`origin` distinguishes `revised_candidate`, `existing_work` and `current_package`. `priority` is one of P1, P2, P3, BUNDLE, DEFER, PRESERVE or INTEGRATE. The first three are proposed commercial sequencing, not automatic execution priority. PRESERVE is explicitly not “start over.”

## Work and commercial state are independent

Allowed work states: planned, deferred, active, blocked, ready_for_test, completed, cancelled, archived, paused, published_reported, operational_reported, prototype_reported, legacy_preserved, needs_reconciliation, package_ready.

Allowed commercial states: unvalidated, published_unvalidated, not_applicable, unknown, unvalidated_catalogue, buyer_signal, paid_pilot, repeat_paid, commercially_validated.

A product can be published and commercially unvalidated. A prototype can pass tests and have no buyers. Internal tooling has no commercial validation requirement. `commercially_validated` must not imply guaranteed future profit; document the exact evidence and remaining uncertainty.

Paid/repeat/commercial validation requires a `validation_evidence_ref` pointing to a non-sensitive reference for reconciled private evidence. Never put receipts, buyer identity or payment details in public records. The validator can require the reference’s presence but **cannot verify the payment**. A human/authorized evidence review still must establish the claim.

`execution_authorized` is descriptive metadata, never an access-control grant. Even setting it true does not authorize a purchase, message, publication or customer-account action. Existing permission systems remain authoritative.

## Resumable body requirements

Keep purpose/buyer, evidence and alternatives, scope/exclusions, acceptance tests, costs/owner labor, completed work, remaining checklist, blocker, next action, decisions, deliverable locations, uncertain external effects and dated work log. Distinguish observed events from estimates. A parent project can have separately tracked components, but do not double-count their hypothetical revenue.

Before resuming: read the whole record and relevant later private checkpoint; inspect the actual owned artifacts; reconcile uncertain external effects; preserve completed work; append new evidence; update one concrete next action. Use one writer per record or compare the expected file hash/version before replacing it. Do not mark old work incomplete merely because it was absent from a new conversation.

## Derived views and integrity

The builder recursively discovers `NICHE.json` and `projects/*.md`, validates identifiers, paths, parents, sources, states and evidence-reference requirements, then generates the index and browser. It makes no network calls and cannot refresh market evidence. It ignores private folders, rejects symlinks, embeds escaped JSON and renders content through DOM text nodes; links allow only safe web/relative destinations. A content-security policy blocks cross-origin connections and forms; the live view polls only its own loopback service.

Rebuild after record changes. `--check` fails on stale/missing generated views and invalid records without writing source files. Generated views include public record bodies; marking a public file “private” is not a substitute for keeping actual sensitive data outside the indexed tree.

`MANIFEST.json` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` describe this delivered snapshot. They are not a runtime signature, encryption or a paid-validation certificate. If Codex edits the package, it must regenerate/reconcile the manifest or label it historical rather than pretend the original hashes still match.


## Revision 2 commercial fields
Schema version 1 remains readable; `commercial_revision: 2` enables stricter optional commercial metadata checks. No project or niche ID changes are needed.

`owner_budget` contains currency (CAD), preferred/planned upfront amounts, authorized spending, cumulative hard ceiling (at most 100), optional itemized envelope and its total, budget fit, review window, recurring owner allocation and production-cost responsibility. A later positive authorization needs an explicit approval reference; data fields do not themselves authorize a tool or payment. Unknown costs must remain unknown until preflight, not silently become zero.

`launch_gate`, `marketing_lane`, `pre_sale_work_cap_hours`, `ad_test_cap_cad`, `production_budget_verified`, `marketing_execution_authorized`, `success_probability` and `offer_price_cad_hypothesis` keep marketing readiness distinct from execution/commercial state. `historical_price_usd_hypothesis` preserves an old proposed price; `offer_price_usd` is null in v2 candidates to prevent treating it as the current quote. Current CAD quotes are editorial hypotheses, not FX conversions or verified buyer acceptance.

`economics_scenarios` and `stress_quote_floor_cad_assumption` are optional explicit sensitivity calculations, not actual financial records. No scenario may populate `actual_revenue`, `actual_profit` or paid-pilot counts. Follow-on AWA-126 points to AWA-095; components retain their parent-only classification. The local validator is not a transaction-control system.


## Live view and public results

`Open_Project_Browser.cmd` starts/reuses the standard-library, read-only loopback service. It rescans public inputs, debounces edits and retains the last valid snapshot on incomplete writes. The browser preserves stable selection, search and expanded niche folders during updates. Generated HTML/JSON remain offline snapshots, not an editable database. Direct HTML opening clearly says live updates require the launcher.

A record may declare up to 20 explicitly public text results:

```json
"public_results": [
  {"label": "Fictional acceptance report", "path": "results/AWA-001/acceptance.md"}
]
```

Use only reviewed, non-sensitive `.md`, `.txt`, `.csv` or `.json` files inside `business_portfolio/results/<the same stable project ID>/`. The record and result file are watched; a new file appears without a browser rebuild. This declaration is not an external publication, spending or filesystem-permission grant. Do not put credentials, real leads/customer documents, private receipts, account information or paid product packages here. The namespace is public planning content, not protected private storage. A narrow secret-pattern check is a safeguard, not privacy certification.

The local service rejects cross-project paths, traversal, symlinks/reparse points, hard-linked files, private folders, unsupported binary releases and recognizable credentials/private buyer links. Files & Results separately labels canonical records/source guides, public results, existing product URLs and withheld/missing assets. Existing arbitrary repository folders are never automatically exposed. Adding another existing asset requires an explicit safe source-guide registry entry and review. No OS folder-open or arbitrary command endpoint exists.

documents.body:
# Verification report — marketing and budget revision
Run date: 2026-11-05. These are **package/planning-tool tests**, not business, customer-workflow or live-account validation.

## Completed checks
- **51 Python regression tests passed**: 31 preserved architecture tests and 20 new commercial/budget/evidence tests. They include 24-level nested niches, IDs/references/cycles, safe parsing/rendering, price arithmetic, missing-cost/approval rejection, separate parent budgets and preserved progress.
- **139 canonical records** pass schema, source-reference and commercial checks. All 126 AWA candidates remain commercially unvalidated; no actual income was added. The 12 existing records keep their prior evidence basis.
- **133 original records compared against the actual earlier ZIP**: work state, commercial validation, actual revenue/profit, paid-pilot fields and completed checkmark lines are unchanged. Newer Windows edits are outside this comparison and must be merged locally.
- **25 browser behavior checks passed** in container Chromium: rendering, ID search, existing-work/recursive-niche filters, budget/launch-gate filters, new projects, report links, pagination, empty results, mobile-width overflow, no JavaScript errors and no external network calls. Desktop and mobile renderings were visually inspected.
- Local Markdown links were checked; exact count and exclusions are recorded in `research/V2_LINK_CHECK.json`. No broken local file targets were found. External URL freshness is not asserted by that link checker.
- The generated browser/index were rebuilt from canonical records and checked for staleness. ZIP CRC integrity and member SHA-256 checks were verified during packaging; the final manifest and checksum list describe this delivery, not the earlier package.

## Explicit limitations and recovery
The default Playwright-managed browser executable was absent. The installed `/usr/bin/chromium` was used instead. Container policy blocked `file://` navigation with `ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ADMINISTRATOR`; the identical generated HTML was loaded as an in-memory browser document for behavioral and rendering tests. Actual direct-file opening in the user's Windows browser remains a local acceptance check. No server is required by the artifact itself.

No n8n/Make/Zapier/client workflow was implemented or executed. Fictional acceptance cases describe future tests, not observed production passes. No advertisement, proposal, customer contact, live storefront edit, native Excel test, charged checkout, refund or payout was performed. No customer conversion, probability of success or income target is established by these tests.

The arithmetic checker verifies local values and declared evidence fields. It cannot validate the authenticity of an approval reference, enforce provider charges, protect a bank account or confer permission. Missing costs/permissions block a proposed request; actual account-level controls and owner approval remain necessary.

Research access varies: 41 revision-specific records are labeled full-page, indexed-primary or connector reads; 67 older records are carried forward, not individually refreshed. Indexed buyer requests are not a confirmed current eligible prospect list. New source evidence does not mark any offer paid or validated.

## Repeat locally
```powershell
python business_portfolio/tools/build_browser.py
python business_portfolio/tools/build_browser.py --check
python business_portfolio/tools/commercial_checks.py --portfolio business_portfolio
python -m unittest discover -s business_portfolio/tests -v
```

Then open the actual Windows `PROJECT_BROWSER.html`, verify its filters/embedded reports and retain any newer local checkpoint before merging. Do not copy historical test counts into a report of tests not actually rerun.

documents.title: Local integration and live explorer — November 5, 2026
documents.body:
# Local integration and live explorer — November 5, 2026

**Ready:** double-click **Open_Project_Browser.cmd** for the simple two-panel project explorer. Its read-only Python standard-library service is available at http://127.0.0.1:22841. Canonical Markdown stays authoritative; live changes appear within a few seconds without rebuilding or reloading. Current portfolio spending authorization remains CAD0. No cloud backend, account, subscription, AI engine or scheduler was added.

**Acceptance limitation:** direct automated file:// opening was denied by the browser URL policy (HTTP/HTTPS only). It was not bypassed. Static HTML was generated and structurally/syntax checked and clearly labels itself a snapshot, but direct-file opening remains an optional owner check. SYS-001 retains that exact blocker rather than claiming every original acceptance criterion passed. No screenshot/native capture was used; live browser DOM and responsive geometry were inspected.

## Implemented

One search field, recursive collapsible project folders, clear names/plain-language states and a readable project pane replace all dashboard statistics, filter dropdowns and report controls. Saved checklists provide completed/current/remaining work. No percentage or financial outcome was invented. Full instructions and the complete original record remain available; research, economics and history are lower collapsible sections. Published products remain distinct from verified paid demand.

`tools/serve_browser.py` debounces file scans, keeps the last valid view during incomplete/invalid writes and uses same-origin polling. Stable selection, search, expanded folders and reasonable scroll position survive updates; stable IDs survive rename/move. The actual Windows CMD launcher starts/reuses the loopback service.

Files & Results labels public source/planning records, explicitly declared public text results, product links and missing/private assets separately. A source guide is not presented as a finished application. `public_results` can declare reviewed text files in `results/<same ID>/`; newly created files appear automatically. Traversal, cross-project paths, private folders, symlinks/reparse points, hard-linked files, unsupported binary releases and recognizable credentials/private buyer URLs are refused. Host/Origin checks prevent cross-origin reads. There is no arbitrary filesystem, OS folder-open, command or write endpoint. Secret-pattern screening is a safeguard, not privacy certification.

## Preserved state and reconciliation

All 139 stable IDs, 81 niche nodes and 108 sources remain, including all 133 original IDs and six additions. No earlier tracked local portfolio existed, and all 345 incoming manifest files matched before edits. Original package/checksum/QA records remain historical snapshot evidence; LOCAL_MANIFEST.json describes the edited local files separately. The extracted package and affected root documents are backed up in the existing ignored `.tmp` area outside the public package; ignored storage is not encryption.

README navigation and a scoped AGENTS checkpoint section were added only in the working tree. HEAD, MERGE_HEAD, the raw Git index, its four staged files and unrelated work were preserved. No commit, push, merge completion/abort, reset, clean or stash occurred. Existing product/research/Bridge/legacy/factory/VaultDesk files and runtime/financial state were unchanged. Completed checklist history and actual financial fields were preserved; only SYS-001 was advanced for observed local work.

EX-001/EX-002 gained dated local reconciliation. Inventory's imported v1.0.1-final claim is explicitly superseded by saved transition evidence and the matching local v1.0.2 archive: 206,757 bytes, SHA-256 0ebab37edde6db94b5ea80bc761dc82133ec6c3637a72e4a8489ac3dda0f23c0. Cleaning's existing v1.0.1 archive matched its saved 61,130-byte/hash evidence. Neither archive was changed, downloaded again or uploaded; private locations/receipt URLs/customer bytes are not embedded.

The source register retains imported access limits: 41 revision sources comprise 9 full-page, 31 indexed-primary and 1 connector read; 67 are carried forward. These are not new research reads or verified live eligible buyers.

## Actual verification

- **Initial integration run: 68 tests, 67 passed, 1 skipped, zero failures/errors.** The subsequent launcher-fix run is recorded below. Real symlink creation lacked Windows privileges; mocked linked-input rejection, real hard-link rejection and the other privacy tests passed. Coverage includes 24-level niches, IDs/references/cycles, malformed metadata, safe text rendering, budget arithmetic and real loopback/watcher lifecycle tests using temporary fictional records.
- Build, stale-output and commercial checks passed for 139 records. Python tools parse; browser JavaScript passes Node syntax checking. Internal links, ID/source coverage, path lengths and credential/private-link patterns are validated separately.
- Live browser checks verified all records, one search/no dropdowns, nested folders, complete instructions, empty results, opening an actual source guide and published-versus-paid/private-asset distinctions. Synthetic creation, instruction/next-step edits, checkbox completion/active status, rename, move/new fourth-level niche, deletion and malformed-write recovery appeared without browser reload. Selection/search/expanded folders remained. A newly created declared public text result appeared and opened automatically. Fixtures were removed.
- At the requested 390px viewport, document width stayed within viewport width and the layout stacked. The temporary viewport override was reset. No browser JavaScript errors were recorded. This is DOM/geometry acceptance, not screenshot visual certification.
- The actual Windows launcher was executed (same launch path as double-click; no physical mouse gesture claimed). Repeating it twice retained one listening service/PID. No dependencies were installed, and no acquisition, charge, order, product/account change, external publication or schedule was created.

## Operational and file-access limits

The service stops at sign-out/restart; the next launcher run starts it again. The corrected launcher reuses the service and requests the page on every intentional run, including after its tab is closed. The default browser may create a new tab; reliable tab detection is unavailable. The earlier suppression of duplicate tabs caused the reopen regression and has been removed. A developer can run the service in a console and stop it with Ctrl+C. No Windows startup task was installed.

Only curated public guides, canonical records and declared non-sensitive text results are exposed. Paid ZIP/XLSX packages, private videos, arbitrary folders, installers and binary assets remain withheld/unverified. A broader existing-asset registry needs a specific safe review; prose paths are not sharing permission. Existing releases and private queues remain intact.

## Next planning action

If selected by the owner, review AWA-005's saved scope and fictional skill-proof specification. That is a planning recommendation from the supplied revision, not a newly verified job, authorization to build client production, send messages or spend. Preserve the published products and reuse existing assets.


## Launcher reopen correction — November 5, 2026

The original existing-service branch returned before requesting the browser. Its deliberate tab-suppression rule caused a CMD window to flash and exit without reopening a closed page. `serve_browser.py --open` now requests the page in both normal reuse and a concurrent bind-race reuse. The new visible `tools/launch_browser.py` checks/reuses the service, logs hidden child startup to `.local/browser-startup.log`, and requests the default browser on every intentional launcher run. The CMD file pauses with a useful error on failure; it works independently of the caller's working directory. No tab-presence detection is assumed, so a default browser may open another tab. One service remains bound to the local port.

The actual updated CMD was launched via normal Windows file association from C:/Windows: it exited with status 0 and retained the same single listening PID. Eight new launcher regression tests passed, including a real CMD failure in a folder with spaces from an unrelated working directory, a visible error/pause path, default-browser failure, existing-service reuse, and the bind-race --open branch. The final full-suite result is 78 tests run: 77 passed, one Windows symlink-creation test skipped, zero failures/errors. The occupied-port test also exposed Windows address reuse; new service starts now request exclusive binding. A real synthetic cold start passed, and a deliberately occupied synthetic port produced the logged startup error. Only synthetic children were stopped; the existing live service was not restarted. Existing canonical records, progress, releases, runtime state, raw Git index and pending merge were preserved.

Normal-browser inspection could not be completed safely: automatic approval review rejected a full accessibility-tree read because unrelated private chats were in that window. That read was not retried or bypassed. The owner then confirmed “yah” when asked whether closing the portfolio tab and double-clicking the updated launcher reopens the live page. This final reopening outcome is owner-confirmed; exit status 0 and a browser-open request alone were not treated as visual proof. No screen capture or denied file:// operation was attempted. Source changes are local only; no commit, push, account/product change or charge occurred.
